title: Site overview
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates a single site in Port Sellow, Alveria, for storage and distribution of packed consumer goods, including food, drugstore products and household items. The site consists of one single-storey warehouse hall with a small attached office annex and a fenced external yard.

2. The warehouse hall provides 6,000 m2 of operational floor space. All storage, handling, picking, packing and dispatch activities take place inside this single hall, which is divided into six defined zones, A to F. No warehousing activity takes place outside the hall except for vehicle movement and dock operations in the yard.

3. The hall has 10 m clear height under the roof structure. This height governs the high-bay racking in bulk storage, the maximum stacking heights for block storage, and the clearance required for all materials-handling equipment. No load, rack or stacked goods may exceed the safe clearances derived from this height.

4. A small office annex is attached to the hall. It houses management, dispatch, administration and welfare facilities. It is separated from warehouse operations and is not used for storage of goods, handling equipment or packing materials.

5. The fenced yard outside the hall covers approximately 3,500 m2. It contains the vehicle circulation areas, manoeuvring space for trailers and vans, the marked driver waiting area, pedestrian crossings and access to all eight dock doors. The fence defines the site boundary and controls entry of vehicles and visitors.

6. The building provides eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height. Doors 1-4 are designated inbound only and serve receiving. Doors 5-8 are designated outbound only and serve dispatch. This separation is fixed and prevents crossing of inbound and outbound flows at the docks.

7. Every carrier is assigned a specific door and time slot by the dispatcher. Drivers report to and remain in the marked waiting area until called to their door. Drivers are not permitted to enter the hall or to wait unapproved in circulation areas.

8. Internal traffic inside the building uses two categories of aisle. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and carry forklift, reach-truck and pallet-jack traffic between zones and to the docks. Rack storage aisles in the bulk-storage area are 3.0 m wide and are dimensioned for high-bay operation.

9. Pedestrian movement is separated from truck traffic. Pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from vehicle aisles by yellow barriers. Crossings, dock ramps and other areas where people and trucks meet are marked and subject to special speed control.

10. Speed limits apply across the whole site and are enforced. The limit is 10 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the yard. A limit of 5 km/h applies wherever people and trucks meet, including marked pedestrian zones, designated crossings and the dock ramps.

11. On entry, every employee, contractor and driver must understand these basic dimensions: 6,000 m2 hall, 3,500 m2 fenced yard, eight docks at 1.2 m height with fixed inbound-outbound split, 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles, 1.2 m segregated walkways, and the 10 / 15 / 5 km/h speed regime. These figures are the basis for all zone layouts, traffic rules and capacity limits described in this manual.

title: Zones A-F
text:
1. The 6,000 m2 hall is divided into six fixed zones, A to F. Each zone has a defined purpose, size and location. Goods, equipment and staff move between zones only in line with the flow described in this manual, and no zone is used for another zone's function.

2. Zone A — receiving, 800 m2. Zone A sits at the inbound end of the hall, directly inside dock doors 1-4. It contains the unloading areas, goods-inspection bays and document-check points. All inbound vehicles are unloaded here, and all inbound paperwork is checked here.

3. Nothing leaves Zone A uninspected and unbooked. Goods remain in Zone A until documents have been checked, quantities counted, condition inspected and the receipt booked into the system. Only then are goods released for put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F.

4. Zone B — bulk storage, 2,200 m2. Zone B is the main storage area and holds high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions. It stores reserve stock for replenishment of the pick faces in Zone C and for other controlled moves. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg.

5. Free block-stacking in Zone B outside the racking is permitted only as defined overflow. It is limited to 3 pallets high and to 4.0 m stacking height. Aisles in Zone B follow the site standard: 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles for high-bay operation.

6. Zone C — picking, 1,200 m2. Zone C contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks. It is the only area where customer order picking takes place. Pick faces are fed by replenishment from bulk storage in Zone B before each picking shift.

7. Zone C is laid out for scanner-directed picking, short travel and separation of pedestrians and trucks. Picked items are scan-verified, packed and labelled before transfer to Zone D. No reserve storage, inbound inspection or outbound loading takes place in Zone C.

8. Zone D — dispatch, 900 m2. Zone D sits at the outbound end of the hall, directly in front of outbound dock doors 5-8. It is used only for staging of finished outbound loads. Only wrapped, labelled pallets assigned to a specific door and load are staged here.

9. Zone D does not store stock. Pallets are staged by door, load and departure sequence, then loaded and sealed under dispatcher release. Empty pallets, packing material and unlabelled goods are not staged in Zone D.

10. Zone E — cold zone, 300 m2. Zone E is a enclosed chilled store held between +2 °C and +8 °C. It stores only goods requiring chilled storage. It is fitted with temperature alarms and is subject to manual temperature verification each shift.

11. Zone F — services and control, 600 m2. Zone F houses value-added packing, quarantine, and returns inspection. Damaged goods found anywhere on site are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day. Returns are inspected here and only then assigned to restock, rework or scrap.

12. Inside Zone F sits a separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. All hazardous goods are stored only in this cage and never elsewhere in the hall. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at any time, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets.

title: Docks and yard
text:
1. The yard and docks form the single interface between road transport and the hall. All vehicles enter, wait, manoeuvre, dock and leave through the fenced yard of about 3,500 m2. No loading or unloading takes place anywhere except at the eight designated dock doors.

2. The building provides eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height. Each door is equipped with its own dock leveller for bridging between the dock edge and the trailer or van bed. Levellers are used for every loading and unloading operation, and no vehicle is serviced at a door whose leveller is tagged out of service.

3. The eight doors are split by direction and the split is fixed. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and open into Zone A receiving. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and open from Zone D dispatch. No inbound delivery is unloaded at an outbound door, and no outbound load is staged or loaded at an inbound door.

4. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling. Every carrier is assigned a specific door and a time slot before arrival. Inbound assignments direct vehicles to Doors 1-4 in line with the receiving plan; outbound assignments direct vehicles to Doors 5-8 in line with the loading sequence. Drivers and warehouse staff do not change doors without dispatcher release.

5. Arrivals report on entry to the site and then wait where directed. A marked driver waiting area is provided in the yard. Drivers remain in that area until called forward to their assigned door and time slot. Waiting in circulation lanes, at unassigned doors, or in the hall is not permitted.

6. Drivers do not enter the hall. Unloading at Doors 1-4 is carried out by inbound operators, and loading at Doors 5-8 is carried out under dispatcher release. Drivers stay with their vehicle or in the waiting area as instructed, except when required at the dock edge for checks under supervision.

7. The yard carries all vehicle circulation, trailer manoeuvring and staging for docking. Lanes are laid out to keep inbound movements toward Doors 1-4 separate from outbound movements toward Doors 5-8 so far as practicable, and to keep pedestrian routes clear at all times.

8. Pedestrian protection applies in the yard as it does inside. Pedestrian walkways and crossings are marked, and the routes between the gate, the waiting area, the office annex and the dock ramps are defined. Where people and trucks meet — at marked crossings, pedestrian zones and the dock ramps — the speed limit is 5 km/h.

9. The general speed limit in the yard is 15 km/h. It applies to forklifts, terminal movements and all road vehicles in circulation and manoeuvring areas. Inside the building the limit is 10 km/h. Both limits drop to 5 km/h at the interfaces listed above, including approach to and departure from the dock ramps.

10. Dock ramps and door aprons are controlled areas. Only the vehicle assigned to that door and the staff handling that load are present during docking, leveller placement, and loading or unloading. Other vehicles and pedestrians do not use or cross a live dock apron.

11. At the end of each dock operation the door area is cleared. Levellers are returned to the stored position, the door is closed, and any pallets, wrap, or equipment are removed from the apron and walkways. A door is only reassigned by the dispatcher once it is clear and ready for the next booked vehicle.

title: Management and supervision
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. is run as a single-site operation under one accountable manager. The warehouse manager, the owner, is accountable for the whole site — operations, safety, inventory accuracy and final sign-offs. Where this manual assigns a decision or approval, it does not remove that overall accountability.

2. Day-to-day authority on the floor is delegated to shift supervision. The company employs 2 shift supervisors to cover the two-shift pattern, morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season. There is always one shift supervisor in charge of the floor during operating hours.

3. Only one person is in charge at any time. When a shift is running, the designated shift supervisor directs all floor staff, sets work priorities within the plan, controls movements between Zones A to F, and is the first point of response for any incident, damage, spill, alarm or evacuation.

4. Handover of command is explicit. At shift change, outgoing and incoming supervisors confirm staffing, active inbound and outbound doors, work in progress in each zone, equipment out of service, and any open incidents or quarantine holds. No shift starts without a supervisor present and briefed.

5. The warehouse manager sets the operating plan, staffing, procedures PR-01 to PR-15, and capacity commitments. The manager confirms the daily labour allocation, approves any overtime, authorises who may operate forklifts, and signs off stocktake results and higher-value write-offs as defined in approvals.

6. The shift supervisor runs each shift within that plan. The supervisor assigns inbound operators, pickers, forklift operators, packing and dispatch tasks by zone and door, enforces aisle discipline, speed limits and PPE, ensures checks before first use of trucks and verifications in the cold zone are done, and stops any unsafe work.

7. Incident response belongs to the supervisor on duty. In case of injury, damage, temperature alarm, spill, fire alarm or evacuation, the supervisor takes charge of the floor, secures the area, accounts for staff, notifies the warehouse manager, and ensures every incident is documented and reviewed before close of shift.

8. Dispatchers and stock controllers advise but do not override floor command. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling and outbound release, and the stock controllers own count tasks and recounts, but movement of people and equipment on the floor during the shift is directed by the shift supervisor.

9. The maintenance technician reports functionally to the warehouse manager and cooperates with the supervisor on duty. Any truck, leveller, rack, wrapper or scanner found unsafe is tagged out, reported to the supervisor, and returned to service only after logged repair. The supervisor ensures tagged equipment is not used.

10. Supervision is visible and available. The shift supervisor remains on the warehouse floor or in the dock area during operating hours, contactable at all times, and is identified to all staff, drivers in the waiting area, and visitors at shift start.

11. In the absence of the warehouse manager, the shift supervisor holds the floor but does not assume owner approvals. Overtime, new forklift authorisations, stocktake sign-off and write-offs above 500 EUR wait for the manager. Where immediate safety requires action beyond delegated authority, the supervisor acts to make safe and reports without delay.

title: Operational roles
text:
1. Day-to-day work on the floor is carried out by fixed operational roles. Each employee works within their trained role and zone, under direction of the shift supervisor on duty. No one undertakes work for which they are not trained, authorised and briefed at shift start.

2. Forklift operators operate materials-handling equipment. The company employs 8 forklift operators to drive the 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. They perform put-away to Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, transfers to Zone D, E and F, and loading and unloading support at the docks.

3. No licence, no truck. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators, and only authorised operators drive trucks. Every truck receives a documented check before its first use each day, and any defect is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician.

4. Inbound operators handle receiving in Zone A. The company employs 6 inbound operators. They unload at inbound Doors 1-4, check documents before unloading is completed, count and inspect goods, and book receipts into the system. Nothing moves past Zone A until they have completed these checks.

5. Pickers handle order picking in Zone C. The company employs 10 pickers. They work only on scanner tasks on the 20 handheld WMS scanners, pick from ground-level pick faces and flow racks, scan-verify every picked item before packing, and pass labelled goods to Zone D. They do not pick from bulk storage or from quarantine.

6. Stock controllers own inventory accuracy day to day. The company employs 2 stock controllers. They run the daily cycle-count programme on the rotating zone schedule, direct recounts, investigate differences between system and rack, and prepare adjustments. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

7. Returns and packing staff work in Zone F. The company employs 4 returns and packing staff. They inspect every return within the 14-day acceptance window, propose restock, rework or scrap for supervisor decision, move damaged goods to quarantine the same day found, and carry out value-added packing work to instruction and label.

8. Dispatchers control transport and outbound flow from the office annex. The company employs 2 dispatchers. They book transport, assign every carrier a door and time slot, direct inbound vehicles to Doors 1-4 and outbound vehicles to Doors 5-8, and release outbound loads from Zone D. No truck is loaded or sealed without dispatcher release.

9. The maintenance technician maintains site equipment. The single technician maintains trucks, racking, dock levellers, stretch wrappers, the baler and scanners, logs every repair, and tags out unsafe equipment. Tagged equipment is not returned to service until repair is logged and cleared.

10. Floaters provide cover for absence. The company employs 2 floaters who are cross-trained for inbound, picking, packing and dispatch support. They are assigned by the shift supervisor where needed and work only within tasks they are trained for. They do not operate forklifts or reach trucks unless separately authorised as forklift operators.

11. Together these roles total about 38 to 40 people with management and supervision: warehouse manager, 2 shift supervisors, 8 forklift operators, 6 inbound operators, 10 pickers, 2 stock controllers, 4 returns and packing staff, 1 maintenance technician, 2 dispatchers and 2 floaters. Staffing on any shift follows the plan set by the warehouse manager and the allocation made by the shift supervisor.

title: Approvals and sign-offs
text:
1. No work moves forward without a defined approval. Every handover between zones, every change to stock figures, every release of a vehicle and every exception requires the sign-off stated in this section. Where a threshold or owner is stated, it is fixed and is not delegated further.

2. The warehouse manager holds all owner approvals for the site. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime, authorises new forklift operators, signs off the annual wall-to-wall stocktake results, and approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR. These four decisions are never taken by another role, even when the manager is absent from the floor.

3. Overtime is approved only in advance by the warehouse manager. This covers extended weekday hours and Saturday morning overtime in peak season. The shift supervisor plans cover with floaters and reallocation within the rostered two shifts, 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00, and escalates any shortfall requiring overtime before it is worked.

4. Forklift authorisation is personal and written. No licence, no truck: only the warehouse manager authorises a new forklift operator for the counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and powered pallet jacks. The daily documented check before first use does not replace this authorisation, and the shift supervisor does not permit any unauthorised driving.

5. The annual stocktake is closed only by the warehouse manager. Cycle counts run every working day under the stock controllers, but the full wall-to-wall stocktake held once a year is signed off personally by the manager. No stocktake result is issued to clients and no post-stocktake adjustment is posted until that signature is recorded.

6. Write-offs for damaged goods are split by value. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager. The threshold applies per incident or per damaged-goods finding, not per unit, and splitting a finding to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

7. The shift supervisor owns three floor decisions on every shift. The supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR, decides the final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap on proposal from returns staff in Zone F, and reviews every incident report before close of shift. Review means confirmation of facts, immediate action taken, and escalation to the manager where required.

8. Returns disposition is decided only after inspection. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery and every unit is inspected in Zone F. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap, and only the shift supervisor approves the final disposition. No return is restocked to Zone B, Zone C or Zone E without that approval.

9. The dispatcher owns dock scheduling and outbound release. Every carrier door assignment for Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound, every time slot, and every release of a wrapped and labelled load from Zone D for loading and sealing requires dispatcher release. Floor staff and drivers do not change doors or load without it.

10. Stock accuracy is protected by a second-count rule. No inventory adjustment is posted without a second count directed by the stock controllers. The second count is independent of the first, and any remaining difference is investigated before an adjustment is prepared for approval under the write-off thresholds above.

11. Damaged goods found anywhere on site are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. The move itself does not need a value approval, but the subsequent write-off or scrap decision follows the thresholds in items 6 and 7. Quarantine holds, racking inspection findings and cold-zone alarms remain open until cleared by the responsible owner and noted in the end-of-shift handover.

title: Shift pattern
text:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates on a fixed two-shift pattern, Monday to Friday. The morning shift runs 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift runs 14:00-22:00. All regular receiving, storage, picking, packing and dispatch work is planned within these two windows.

2. The site is staffed only when a shift is running and a supervisor is present. There is always one shift supervisor in charge of the floor during operating hours. No shift starts without its designated supervisor briefed and present, and command passes explicitly at changeover.

3. The two shifts cover the full flow through Zones A to F. Morning shift typically takes the first inbound arrivals at Doors 1-4, completes put-away to Zone B, E and F, and replenishes Zone C pick faces. Afternoon shift continues inbound and replenishment, completes picking, packing and outbound loading from Zone D at Doors 5-8, and closes the day.

4. Standard working hours are 06:00-22:00 on weekdays, split as above. Outside these hours the hall is closed for operations. Any vehicle, contractor or overtime work outside 06:00-22:00 Monday to Friday requires prior approval as overtime under the rule below.

5. Saturday working is overtime only and applies in peak season only. When authorised, it is limited to a Saturday morning shift. There is no regular Saturday afternoon, Sunday or night operation, and no standing weekend roster.

6. Overtime is never self-authorised and never assumed. Only the warehouse manager approves overtime, in advance. This covers any extension beyond the rostered 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and any Saturday morning working in peak season.

7. The shift supervisor manages cover within the roster before requesting overtime. Absence is covered first by reallocation within the shift and by assignment of the 2 cross-trained floaters to inbound, picking, packing or dispatch support. Only when cover cannot be met inside the roster does the supervisor escalate to the manager.

8. Staffing on each shift follows the plan set by the warehouse manager. From the total of about 38-40 people — manager, 2 shift supervisors, 8 forklift operators, 6 inbound operators, 10 pickers, 2 stock controllers, 4 returns and packing staff, 1 maintenance technician, 2 dispatchers and 2 floaters — the supervisor allocates trained staff by zone and door for that shift.

9. Each of the 2 shift supervisors normally leads the same shift, mornings or afternoons, to preserve continuity on doors, zones and client orders. Peak-season Saturday morning overtime is led by a designated supervisor, with staffing limited to the tasks approved in the overtime request.

10. Shift discipline is fixed. Staff work only their assigned shift, zone and role, start and finish on time, and hand over live work at 14:00 and at 22:00 under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Work left unfinished at end of shift remains in its zone, secured and recorded, until the next responsible shift takes it up.

11. Operating outside the pattern does not change responsibility. Evening close, Saturday overtime close and any approved extension are handed over, secured and recorded in the same way as a weekday shift, with open doors, quarantine holds, alarms and equipment defects carried forward until cleared by the responsible owner.

title: End-of-shift handover
text:
1. Every shift ends with a formal handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Handover is a face-to-face exchange between the outgoing and incoming shift supervisor, with input from dispatch, stock control and the floor leads. Work is not considered handed over until it is recorded and acknowledged.

2. Command transfers only at the handover point. The morning shift hands over at 14:00 and the afternoon shift hands over at 22:00, or at the close of any approved overtime. The incoming supervisor must be present and briefed before taking charge of the floor, and the outgoing supervisor remains responsible until that point.

3. The handover covers staffing and doors. The supervisors confirm who is present, absent and assigned as cover, which of inbound Doors 1-4 and outbound Doors 5-8 are live, booked or closed, which carriers are waiting, delayed or due next shift, and any dispatcher changes to doors or time slots.

4. The handover covers work in progress by zone. Zone A receipts part-unloaded or awaiting document check, count or booking; Zone B put-away and Zone C replenishment outstanding; Zone C picking tasks open or part-picked; Zone D pallets staged, wrapped or awaiting dispatcher release; Zone F returns under inspection, value-added packing in progress, and quarantine holds are all stated by location and quantity.

5. The handover carries forward cold-zone and controlled stock. The manual temperature verification for Zone E for the shift just ending is confirmed as done, with any alarm or deviation noted. The hazmat cage quantity against its 4,000 kg limit and any spill-kit use under PR-13 are reported, as is any damaged-goods move to quarantine that day.

6. The handover carries forward equipment status. Every truck checked before first use that day, any truck, leveller, wrapper, baler or WMS scanner tagged out of service, and any rack damage found are listed. Tagged equipment remains out of use until logged repair and clearance by the maintenance technician, and the incoming shift must not use it.

7. The handover closes incidents for the shift. Every injury, near miss, damage, temperature alarm, spill, fire alarm or evacuation element is reported, with immediate action taken and area secured. The outgoing supervisor reviews every incident report before close of shift, confirms facts and escalation to the warehouse manager, and the incoming supervisor accepts any open follow-up.

8. Stock accuracy items are handed over explicitly. Cycle counts completed that day, recounts pending, second counts required before any adjustment, and findings for racking inspection or annual stocktake preparation are stated. No adjustment is handed over as agreed unless the second-count rule has been met.

9. The handover is written down. The outgoing supervisor records doors, zone WIP, quarantine and hazmat status, equipment out of service, incidents and open actions in the shift log. The incoming supervisor signs acknowledgement, adds staffing and priorities for the next shift, and notes any matter requiring warehouse manager decision, including overtime or write-offs above 500 EUR.

10. Unfinished work is left safe and identifiable. Goods remain in their zone, secured clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways. Zone D staging stays by door and load, levellers are stored and doors closed when not live, and pedestrian barriers and markings are left in place.

11. If the next operating shift does not start immediately, the close is still handed over. Evening close at 22:00 and Saturday morning overtime close secure the hall, yard and office annex, leave open doors, holds, alarms and defects recorded in the log, and name the responsible owner for each item until the next briefed supervisor takes charge.

title: Per-shift checks
text:
1. Every shift starts with checks, not with work. The shift supervisor confirms that a briefed supervisor is present, staffing by zone and door is assigned, and the previous handover under PR-15 has been read and acknowledged. No inbound unloading at Doors 1-4, no picking in Zone C and no loading at Doors 5-8 starts until these confirmations are recorded in the shift log.

2. Trucks are checked before they are used. Every counterbalance forklift, reach truck and electric pallet jack receives a documented check before its first use each day, covering brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains, guarding, battery charge and visible damage. The morning shift completes the full record; the afternoon shift re-confirms status at 14:00 handover and re-checks any truck newly brought into service.

3. Any truck found defective is stopped immediately. The supervisor tags it out, informs the maintenance technician, and records it in the handover. Tagged trucks, levellers, wrappers or scanners are not used until repair is logged and clearance is given. Seat belts on forklifts are checked as part of this check and worn whenever the truck is moving.

4. The cold zone is verified manually each shift. In Zone E the supervisor or assigned operator reads the independent thermometer, confirms the store is between +2 °C and +8 °C, checks the alarm panel for active or silenced alarms, and records time, reading and initials. Any deviation or alarm is treated under PR-12, stock is held, and the warehouse manager is notified without delay.

5. Controlled stock is counted by eye each shift. The hazmat cage in Zone F is checked against its 4,000 kg limit, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets, with no product outside the 60 m2 ventilated cage. Quarantine holds and returns awaiting inspection are confirmed present, labelled and segregated, and any damaged goods found since last handover are confirmed moved the same day.

6. Doors and docks are checked before booking in carriers. The supervisor and dispatcher confirm which of inbound Doors 1-4 and outbound Doors 5-8 are live, that each leveller operates and returns to stored position, that aprons and 1.2 m walkways are clear, and that drivers are held in the marked waiting area. No door with a tagged-out leveller is assigned.

7. Aisles and pedestrian separation are walked each shift. Main transport aisles are confirmed clear to 4.0 m, rack aisles in Zone B to 3.0 m, and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers are confirmed unobstructed. Crossings, dock ramps and pedestrian zones are checked for markings and for the 5 km/h regime, with the general 10 km/h inside and 15 km/h in the yard enforced.

8. People readiness is checked at shift start. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are confirmed for everyone on the floor, with no exceptions, and only operators authorised by the warehouse manager are assigned to forklifts, reach trucks and powered pallet jacks. Floaters are assigned only to tasks they are trained for.

9. Systems and packing equipment are confirmed ready. The 20 handheld WMS scanners are checked for charge and login, the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and the cardboard baler are confirmed serviceable, and pick faces in Zone C are confirmed replenished from bulk before picking tasks are released under PR-03 and PR-04.

10. Zone readiness closes the opening checks. Zone A is confirmed clear for new arrivals with no unbooked stock carried over unrecorded; Zone C is confirmed free of reserve storage and quarantine goods; Zone D holds only wrapped, labelled pallets by door and load. Open cycle counts, second counts pending and rack damage are carried forward for the stock controllers.

11. Each shift ends as it began, with verification. At 14:00 and at 22:00, or at close of approved Saturday overtime, the supervisor confirms temperature verification done, equipment defects tagged, incidents reviewed, and unfinished work left secured clear of aisles and walkways. Open items remain named to an owner in the log until cleared.

title: Arrival and scheduling
text:
1. All inbound arrivals are planned before the truck reaches the site. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific inbound door from Doors 1-4 and a time slot, and shares the receiving plan with the shift supervisor. No inbound vehicle arrives unbooked or is directed to a door on arrival by the driver.

2. Doors 1-4 are inbound only and open into Zone A receiving. They are the only doors where unloading takes place. Inbound vehicles are never assigned to outbound Doors 5-8, and outbound loads are never handled at an inbound door, even when an inbound door is idle.

3. Each inbound slot corresponds to a defined receipt in Zone A. The dispatcher sequences arrivals to match unloading capacity, inspection bays and put-away availability in Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Overlapping bookings that would block the 4.0 m main aisles or overflow the 800 m2 receiving area are not released.

4. On arrival at the gate, the driver reports to the assigned door and time slot. The dispatcher or supervisor confirms identity, carrier, purchase order or delivery reference, and assigned door. Vehicles that are early or late hold as directed and do not proceed to a door until called forward.

5. Waiting drivers remain in the marked waiting area in the fenced yard. Drivers do not wait in circulation lanes, at unassigned doors or dock aprons, and never enter the hall. They move to the dock edge only when called to their slot and only as instructed for checks under supervision.

6. Yard movement to the door follows site traffic rules. The limit is 15 km/h in the yard, dropping to 5 km/h at marked pedestrian zones, crossings and the dock ramps. Only the vehicle assigned to a live door and the staff handling that receipt are present at the apron during docking and leveller placement.

7. A door is made ready before the vehicle is called. The supervisor confirms the leveller operates and returns to stored position, the apron and 1.2 m walkway are clear, inbound operators are assigned, and previous receipts are cleared from the bay. No vehicle is docked at a door whose leveller is tagged out of service.

8. Documents are checked first, before anything is unloaded, under PR-01 Inbound receiving. The inbound operator verifies delivery note, order reference, quantities advised, batch and expiry where applicable, and cold-chain or hazmat paperwork for Zone E or Zone F goods. Unloading does not start until the paperwork check is passed.

9. If documents are missing, incorrect or do not match the booking, the load stays on the vehicle. The inbound operator holds the receipt in Zone A status, informs the shift supervisor and dispatcher, and the vehicle waits or is rescheduled as directed. Nothing moves past Zone A until the paperwork is checked and recorded.

10. Once documents are accepted, unloading, counting and inspection proceed in Zone A. Inbound operators unload at the assigned door, count and inspect condition, and record damage or shortage immediately. Only inspected goods are booked into the system, and only booked goods are released for put-away.

11. Every arrival is closed in the log. Door, slot time, actual arrival and departure, document result, quantities received and any hold for quarantine, cold-zone verification or dispatcher rescheduling are recorded and carried into the end-of-shift handover. An unbooked or unchecked receipt is never treated as stock.

title: Unloading and inspection
text:
1. Unloading takes place only at the assigned inbound door from Doors 1-4 and only after the document check under PR-01 Inbound receiving has been passed. No pallet, carton or parcel is removed from the vehicle until the inbound operator confirms paperwork, booking reference and door assignment. If paperwork fails, the load stays on the trailer.

2. Unloading is carried out by inbound operators in Zone A receiving, supported by forklift operators as directed by the shift supervisor. Drivers do not enter the hall and do not unload. Drivers remain with the vehicle or as instructed at the dock edge under supervision while operators handle all goods inside the 800 m2 receiving area.

3. Every dock operation uses the door leveller. The leveller is placed only for the assigned vehicle, chocks and brakes are confirmed, and the 5 km/h regime at the dock ramp is observed. No unloading starts at a door whose leveller is tagged out of service, and the apron is kept clear of other vehicles and pedestrians.

4. Goods are unloaded directly into the Zone A inspection bays by load and delivery line. Pallets are placed clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and the 1.2 m segregated walkways behind yellow barriers. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg, and any pallet showing collapse, leaning or wrap failure is secured before further movement.

5. Counting is done at unloading, not later. Inbound operators count quantities by pallet, carton and unit as applicable, reconcile against the delivery note and order quantity, and record shortage, overage or mis-pick immediately. Count results are entered on the receipt record in Zone A and carried forward to booking.

6. Inspection follows count on the same receipt. Operators check outer packaging, labelling, batch and expiry date where applicable, cleanliness, and visible damage or leakage. For chilled goods for Zone E, transport temperature evidence and product condition are checked on arrival before transfer to the cold zone. For hazmat for Zone F, labels, closures and integrity are checked without opening containers.

7. Only inspected goods are booked into the system. Goods that have not been counted and inspected remain in Zone A status and are not moved to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Only booked goods are released for put-away under PR-02, and the system receipt is created only for the quantity verified as correct and undamaged.

8. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming goods are segregated immediately. Anything found damaged, wet, open, expired, mislabelled or otherwise unfit is marked, recorded and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day it is found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. It is never put away to bulk, cold or pick stock and never left in Zone A unrecorded overnight.

9. Cold-zone and hazmat receipts follow controlled routing. Chilled goods accepted in Zone A are moved promptly to Zone E, held between +2 °C and +8 °C with alarm cover, and subject to shift verification. Hazmat goods are moved only to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F, never stored elsewhere, and counted against the 4,000 kg limit, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets.

10. Returns delivered to an inbound door are not treated as inbound receipts. Any return arriving at Doors 1-4 is identified at document check and transferred to Zone F for handling under PR-07. It is accepted only within 14 days of delivery, every unit is inspected there, and no return is restocked without shift-supervisor disposition.

11. Each receipt is closed in Zone A before the door is released. The inbound operator confirms pallets cleared from the bay, count and inspection recorded, system booking completed or hold noted, quarantine moves done, and leveller stored and door closed. Open holds, shortages and damage are entered in the shift log for handover and dispatcher follow-up.

title: Booking and release
text:
1. Booking is the moment inspected goods become system stock. No pallet or carton in Zone A is treated as available stock until its receipt has been created in the WMS. Only inspected goods are booked into the system, and only booked goods are released for put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F.

2. Booking follows count and inspection on the same receipt under PR-01 Inbound receiving. The inbound operator confirms documents checked, quantities counted, condition inspected and shortages, overages or damage recorded. Any line not verified as correct and undamaged is excluded from the booking and held or segregated in Zone A status.

3. Booking is carried out by inbound operators on the handheld WMS scanners. Each scan creates the system receipt by purchase order or delivery reference, supplier, item, batch and expiry where applicable, quantity, pallet ID and destination zone. Manual entry without scan verification is not permitted.

4. The booked quantity is the verified quantity, not the advised quantity. Shortages and overages against the delivery note are recorded at booking and flagged to the dispatcher for supplier follow-up. Damaged, wet, open, expired or mislabelled units found at inspection are not included in the booked quantity and are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

5. Every booked pallet receives its system pallet label in Zone A before it moves. The label shows item, quantity, batch and expiry, pallet ID and destination location class. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg, and any pallet without a readable label remains in Zone A and is not released for put-away.

6. Release to put-away is a separate step after booking under PR-02 Put-away to storage. The shift supervisor or inbound lead confirms the booking is complete, labels are applied, and forklift capacity is available. Only then are booked pallets directed out of the 800 m2 receiving area clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways.

7. Release specifies destination by goods type. Ambient reserve stock is released to Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 pallet positions. Chilled goods are released promptly to Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C. Hazmat goods are released only to the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F, counted against the 4,000 kg limit. Value-added, quarantine or returns-related holds are released only to Zone F.

8. Controlled receipts are verified at release. For Zone E, transport temperature evidence and condition recorded at arrival are attached to the booking before movement. For hazmat, labels, closures and integrity are confirmed without opening containers, and cage capacity for 4 full-weight pallets is confirmed before release. If cold or cage capacity is unavailable, booked pallets wait secured in Zone A and are carried in the handover.

9. Nothing unbooked leaves Zone A. Uninspected goods, paperwork holds, returns identified at document check for transfer to Zone F under PR-07, and goods awaiting recount are never released to Zone B, Zone C, Zone D or Zone E. Reserve pallets are never sent direct to Zone C pick faces or Zone D staging at this stage.

10. The inbound door is released only when its receipts are booked or formally held. The inbound operator confirms pallets labelled and cleared, bookings posted, quarantine moves recorded, leveller returned to stored position and door closed. The dispatcher then reassigns Doors 1-4 for the next booked carrier.

11. Every booking and release is recorded for handover. Receipt number, door, booked versus advised quantity, pallet IDs, destination zone, holds and quarantine moves are entered in the shift log. Open holds, shortages and damage carry forward under PR-15 until put-away is confirmed, and no adjustment to a booking is posted without a second count.

title: Bulk storage put-away
text:
1. Only booked goods are put away to Zone B. No pallet leaves Zone A receiving until documents have been checked, quantities counted, condition inspected and the system receipt created in the WMS under PR-01. Unbooked, unlabelled or held goods are never directed to bulk storage.

2. Put-away to Zone B runs under PR-02 Put-away to storage. The shift supervisor confirms booking is complete and pallet labels are applied, then assigns a forklift operator with a WMS-directed location. Put-away is scanner-directed throughout, using the 20 handheld WMS scanners, and manual placement without scan confirmation is not permitted.

3. Zone B is the 2,200 m2 bulk storage area with high-bay pallet racking providing 2,400 pallet positions. It holds ambient reserve stock for replenishment of Zone C pick faces. Chilled, hazmat, quarantine and returns stock are never put away to Zone B and are routed only to Zone E or Zone F.

4. All high-bay put-away is performed with reach trucks rated at 1.6 t or counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, as directed for the aisle and height. Only operators authorised by the warehouse manager drive trucks. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg, and that limit is observed on every lift and placement.

5. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg. The operator confirms bay capacity before placement and never exceeds it, even where a pallet position is physically free. In practice this limits a bay to two full-weight 1,000 kg pallets plus allowance, and loading beyond the bay plate is stopped and reported to the supervisor and maintenance technician.

6. Placement follows the scanner task to the exact beam location, level and pallet ID. The operator scans the pallet label and the location label, places the pallet squarely on the beams without overhang or contact with uprights, and confirms completion by scan. Any mismatch between system location and physical location is held and reported to the stock controllers.

7. Rack aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide and are dimensioned for high-bay operation. Main transport aisles feeding Zone B are 4.0 m wide. The speed limit is 10 km/h inside, with seat belts worn whenever the truck is moving and pedestrian walkways of 1.2 m behind yellow barriers kept clear at all times.

8. Free block-stacking outside the racking is overflow only and is used only when directed by the shift supervisor. It is limited to 3 pallets high and to 4.0 m stacking height. Block stacks are placed square, stable and wrapped, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways, and never against rack uprights, dock ramps or fire exits.

9. Damaged or suspect pallets found during put-away are not racked. Any pallet showing collapse, leaning, broken boards, wrap failure or leakage is secured where found, recorded, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Racking damage or unsafe beams found during placement are tagged, reported immediately, and left unused until logged repair.

10. Put-away is confirmed by scan before the pallet becomes available reserve. The completed scan updates the WMS with location, pallet ID, quantity, batch and expiry where applicable. Pallets not confirmed as stored are not offered for replenishment to Zone C and remain listed as in transit from Zone A until resolved.

11. Every put-away movement is recorded for handover. Receipt number, pallet IDs, locations used, overflow block-stack positions, quarantine moves and rack damage are entered in the shift log under PR-15. Outstanding put-away waits secured in Zone A, clear of aisles and walkways, and is carried forward until confirmed stored.

title: Cold-zone storage
text:
1. Zone E is the 300 m2 enclosed chilled store for goods requiring chilled storage. It holds only chilled product between +2 °C and +8 °C. No ambient, hazmat, quarantine or returns stock is stored in Zone E, and no chilled stock is stored elsewhere in the hall.

2. Chilled storage runs under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and PR-02 Put-away to storage. Only booked goods are put away to Zone E. Goods remain in Zone A receiving until documents, count, condition and transport temperature evidence have been checked, and only inspected goods are booked into the WMS before movement.

3. Transfer from Zone A to Zone E is prompt. Chilled pallets labelled in Zone A are moved without delay, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m segregated walkways, with doors to Zone E kept closed except for the move. Booked pallets waiting for cold space wait secured in Zone A and are carried in the shift log.

4. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg in Zone E as elsewhere. Pallets are placed only in designated chilled locations by WMS-directed task, confirmed by scan of pallet and location labels. Manual placement without scan confirmation is not permitted, and unlabelled pallets are never released to Zone E.

5. The store is held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C with alarm cover. The enclosure, doors, seals and refrigeration are kept closed and intact. Doors are opened only for put-away, replenishment to Zone C, count or inspection, and are closed immediately after each movement.

6. Temperature is verified manually each shift. The supervisor or assigned operator reads the independent thermometer, confirms +2 °C to +8 °C, checks the alarm panel for active or silenced alarms, and records time, reading and initials. Morning and afternoon shifts each record their own verification under PR-15.

7. Any deviation or alarm stops normal flow. On alarm, out-of-range reading or door failure, stock is held, no further put-away or issue to picking takes place, and the shift supervisor takes charge. The warehouse manager is notified without delay, and product is not released until condition is assessed under PR-12.

8. Handling inside Zone E follows cold-chain discipline. Forklift operators and pallet-jack movements observe 10 km/h inside and seat-belt use, with only operators authorised by the warehouse manager driving powered trucks. Exposure time is minimised, and chilled pallets are never staged in ambient zones except for immediate transfer.

9. Replenishment of chilled pick faces and picking of chilled orders are drawn only from verified Zone E stock. No expired, damaged, wet or open product is issued. Anything found damaged or suspect during put-away, count or picking is segregated, recorded and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

10. Inventory in Zone E is covered by the same accuracy rules as bulk storage. Cycle counts run on the rotating schedule under PR-08, recounts are directed by the stock controllers, and no adjustment is posted without a second count. Returns are restocked to Zone E only after inspection in Zone F and shift-supervisor disposition.

11. Every chilled movement and check is recorded for handover. Receipt numbers, pallet IDs, locations, temperature readings, alarms, holds and quarantine moves are entered in the shift log. Open alarms, held stock and unresolved deviations remain named to an owner until cleared, and roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until closed.

title: Hazmat cage and quarantine
text:
1. Zone F services and control, 600 m2, contains two strictly separated controlled stores: quarantine for damaged, suspect and held goods, and a separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. Both are managed under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. No other zone holds quarantine or hazmat stock.

2. The hazmat cage holds all hazardous goods on site and nothing else. Hazmat is never stored elsewhere in the hall, in Zone A, B, C, D or E, in walkways, on dock aprons or in the yard. Any hazmat pallet found outside the cage is moved immediately under supervisor direction and reported as an incident.

3. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at any time, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Before any booked hazmat receipt is released from Zone A, the shift supervisor confirms remaining cage capacity by weight and by pallet positions. If capacity is unavailable, booked pallets wait secured in Zone A and are carried in the handover.

4. The cage is enclosed, lockable, ventilated and marked. Access is limited to trained staff assigned by the shift supervisor. Incompatible products are segregated inside to instruction, containers are kept closed, upright and labelled, and are never opened inside the cage except under PR-13. Smoking, charging and hot work are prohibited at the cage.

5. Put-away to the cage runs under PR-02 and PR-13. Only booked, labelled hazmat goods inspected in Zone A are moved, by WMS scan of pallet and cage location, using authorised operators and intact pallets and wrap. Labels, closures and integrity are confirmed without opening containers. Unlabelled or leaking units are not racked but segregated as quarantine.

6. The cage is checked visually each shift. The supervisor confirms quantity against the 4,000 kg limit, segregation and labelling intact, ventilation running, spill kits present and unused, and no product outside the 60 m2 boundary. Readings, quantities and any spill-kit use are entered in the shift log and handed over under PR-15.

7. Spill response starts at the cage. On leakage, odour, damaged container or spill alarm the area is secured, people kept clear, ignition sources removed, and the shift supervisor takes charge. Cleanup uses only the dedicated spill kits and PPE to PR-13 instruction. Contaminated material is treated as quarantine and the warehouse manager is notified without delay.

8. Quarantine in Zone F holds all damaged, suspect, expired, mislabelled and non-conforming goods, and all returns and deviations awaiting decision. It is physically separate from the hazmat cage, from value-added packing and from returns inspection, and is clearly marked and bounded. Conforming reserve, pick or dispatch stock is never placed in quarantine.

9. Damaged goods found anywhere on site are moved to quarantine the same day they are found. The finder secures the pallet where found clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways, informs the supervisor, and it is transferred, labelled with date, origin zone, receipt or order reference, reason and finder initials. It remains system-blocked until disposition.

10. Nothing leaves quarantine without approval. Returns staff inspect and propose restock, rework or scrap, and only the shift supervisor decides final disposition. Write-offs up to and including 500 EUR are approved by the supervisor; write-offs above 500 EUR are reserved to the warehouse manager. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

11. Every cage and quarantine movement is recorded for handover. Receipt numbers, pallet IDs, weights against the 4,000 kg limit, quarantine labels, inspections, dispositions, spill events and tag-outs are entered in the shift log. Open quarantine holds, cage over-limit risks and uncleared spills remain named to an owner and roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared and logged as repaired.

title: Replenishment of pick faces
text:
1. Zone C pick faces are fed only from bulk reserve under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. No pick face in the 1,200 m2 picking area is filled direct from Zone A receiving, from Zone D dispatch, or from quarantine in Zone F. Only confirmed reserve from Zone B, and verified stock from Zone E for chilled lines, is moved to Zone C.

2. Replenishment runs before each picking shift. The outgoing and incoming work is planned so that ground-level pick faces and flow racks are filled before picker scanner tasks under PR-04 are released. Picking does not start on a shift until the shift supervisor confirms replenishment for that shift is complete or formally carried as shortage.

3. Need is set by the WMS, not by eye. The system generates replenishment tasks from open customer orders, minimum and maximum levels per pick face, and available reserve quantity. Pickers do not call for stock themselves and forklift operators do not move reserve without a scanner task.

4. Tasks are assigned by the shift supervisor to authorised forklift operators. Movements from Zone B high-bay racking use reach trucks rated at 1.6 t or counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t as directed for aisle and height. Only operators authorised by the warehouse manager drive powered trucks, and every move is confirmed on the 20 handheld WMS scanners.

5. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg on every replenishment move. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg, and bay plates are observed on withdrawal as on put-away. Stock is taken from the exact beam location stated in the task, confirmed by scan of location and pallet ID before the pallet is broken down or moved.

6. Travel follows site traffic rules. Main transport aisles are used at 4.0 m width between Zone B and Zone C, rack aisles in Zone B at 3.0 m, with 10 km/h inside and seat belts worn whenever the truck is moving. The 1.2 m pedestrian walkways behind yellow barriers are kept clear, and pallets are never staged in aisles or on walkways during transfer.

7. Replenishment to the face is by scan to location. The operator scans the reserve pallet and the pick-face location, places only the quantity tasked, faces labels forward, and confirms completion by scan. Overfilling of flow racks, mixing of batches or expiry dates in one face, and placement without scan confirmation are not permitted.

8. Chilled pick faces are replenished only from verified Zone E stock held between +2 C and +8 C. Transfer is prompt with Zone E doors closed immediately after the move, and exposure in ambient areas is limited to immediate transfer. No expired, damaged or alarmed stock is issued, and any deviation in Zone E holds all chilled replenishment until cleared under PR-12.

9. Hazmat, quarantine and returns stock are never used for replenishment. Goods in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage counted against the 4,000 kg limit, goods blocked in quarantine in Zone F, and returns awaiting supervisor disposition are system-blocked and are not offered to Zone C even when a pick face is empty.

10. Damage found during replenishment stops that line. A collapsed pallet, broken boards, wrap failure, leakage or rack damage is secured where found clear of aisles and walkways, reported to the supervisor and maintenance technician, and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. The pick face is left empty and flagged until conforming reserve is supplied.

11. Every replenishment is recorded for handover under PR-15. Tasks completed, faces still short, reserve shortages in Zone B or Zone E, quarantine moves and rack damage are entered in the shift log. Unfilled faces and outstanding reserve moves roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00, and no inventory adjustment arising from a short face is posted without a second count directed by the stock controllers.

title: Order picking
text:
1. Order picking takes place only in Zone C under PR-04 Order picking. The 1,200 m2 picking area with ground-level pick faces and flow racks is the only area where customer orders are picked. No picking takes place from bulk racking in Zone B, from quarantine in Zone F, or from staging in Zone D.

2. Picking starts only after replenishment is confirmed. Before picker scanner tasks are released on a shift, the shift supervisor confirms that pick faces have been replenished from Zone B bulk reserve, and from verified Zone E stock for chilled lines, under PR-03. Picking does not start on short faces except as formally carried shortage.

3. Picking is scanner-directed throughout. The company employs 10 pickers who work only on tasks issued to the 20 handheld WMS scanners. Verbal instruction, paper lists and picking to memory are not permitted. A picker logs on, accepts the task offered, and follows the system sequence by location, item and quantity.

4. Tasks are assigned by the shift supervisor by zone and priority. Pickers work within their assigned aisles and orders, keep to the 1.2 m segregated walkways behind yellow barriers for foot travel, and use hand pallet jacks or electric pallet jacks for small moves. Only operators authorised by the warehouse manager drive powered trucks.

5. Each pick is scan-verified at the face. The picker scans the pick-face location label and then each item or carton picked, confirms batch and expiry where applicable, and enters quantity on the scanner. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed. A pick without a successful scan is not a completed pick and is not passed forward.

6. Shorts, damage and label mismatches stop that line. If the face is empty, short, damaged, mislabelled or shows mixed batch or expiry, the picker leaves the task open on the scanner, flags the face, and informs the supervisor and stock controllers. The picker does not take substitute stock from reserve, hazmat or quarantine, and does not complete the order short without system instruction.

7. Picked goods are packed and labelled before transfer. After scan verification, items are packed to instruction, cartons closed and labelled with order, item, quantity and destination. Unlabelled or incompletely verified goods are never moved to Zone D. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg when picks are consolidated to pallet.

8. Transfer to Zone D is by completed order or pallet only. Labelled picks are moved clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 1.2 m walkways to the dispatch area in front of Doors 5-8. Zone D holds only wrapped, labelled pallets by door and load, and picking trolleys, empty pallets and packing waste are cleared from the transfer route.

9. Chilled picks follow cold-chain discipline under PR-12. Chilled orders are picked only from verified Zone E-fed faces held between +2 °C and +8 °C, with exposure in ambient areas limited to immediate picking and transfer. On any Zone E alarm or deviation, chilled picking on that line is held until cleared by the supervisor and warehouse manager.

10. Safety and order are maintained during picking. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory with no exceptions, the 10 km/h inside limit applies to all truck and jack movements, and flow racks are never overfilled, climbed or used for reserve storage. Damaged goods found at the face are secured clear of aisles and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

11. Every picking shift is recorded for handover under PR-15. Tasks completed, orders part-picked, faces still short, reserve shortages passed to replenishment, scanner faults and quarantine moves are entered in the shift log. Open tasks and staged pallets roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until packed, labelled and accepted in Zone D, and no adjustment for a picking difference is posted without a second count.

title: Packing and labelling
text:
1. Packing and labelling runs under PR-05 Packing and labelling and covers the step between picking in Zone C and staging in Zone D. No picked goods enter Zone D dispatch unless they have been scan-checked, packed, labelled and, where palletised, wrapped. Unlabelled or unwrapped pallets are never staged in front of Doors 5-8.

2. Only scan-verified picks are packed. Every picked item is scan-verified at the pick face in Zone C before it is packed, by scan of location and item on the handheld WMS scanners. A pick without a successful scan is not passed to the packing bench and is held open for the supervisor and stock controllers.

3. Packing is to instruction and order. Packers confirm order, item, quantity, batch and expiry where applicable against the scanner task, use the specified carton size and fill, close and seal cartons, and separate orders and customers. Mixing of orders in one carton or pallet without system direction is not permitted.

4. Cartons and pallets are built stable and within limit. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Goods are stacked square without overhang, heavy items below light items, labels outward, and unstable builds are re-stacked before wrapping. Any pallet showing collapse, leaning or wrap failure is secured and not released.

5. Every carton, parcel and pallet is labelled before transfer. Labels show order, customer, item, quantity, pallet ID, batch and expiry where applicable, and destination door and load when assigned. Labels are applied flat, readable and scannable, one set per unit. Units without a readable label remain at packing and are not moved to Zone D.

6. Label checks are by scan, not by eye alone. The packer scans the packed label against the order task to confirm match before release. Mismatches, short quantities, damaged cartons or mislabelled faces stop that order line, which is flagged and reported to the shift supervisor. Substitute stock from reserve, hazmat or quarantine is never used.

7. Palletised loads are wrapped in Zone D entry on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Wrapping covers base to top with sufficient turns to bind load to pallet, with corners and top layer secured. Dispatch confirms wrappers serviceable each shift, and loads not passing wrap check are re-wrapped. No unwrapped pallet is staged by door.

8. Packing waste is cleared at source. Cardboard offcuts, backing and damaged cartons go directly to the cardboard baler, and plastic, strapping and packing waste are segregated to bins. Transfer routes via the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m segregated walkways behind yellow barriers are kept clear, and empty pallets are returned to defined stacks.

9. Chilled and controlled lines follow their routing. Chilled packs from verified Zone E-fed faces held between +2 °C and +8 °C are packed with minimum ambient exposure and moved promptly to Zone D. Hazmat and quarantine stock are never packed as outbound product, and returns are restocked only after inspection in Zone F and supervisor disposition.

10. Damage found at packing is segregated immediately. Damaged, wet, open, expired or mislabelled units are marked, recorded and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. They are never packed, labelled as conforming, or included in a dispatch pallet to make up quantity.

11. Every packing shift is recorded for handover under PR-15. Orders packed, pallets labelled and wrapped, wrapper and baler status, scanner faults, quarantine moves and orders held short are entered in the shift log. Completed wrapped and labelled pallets roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 for staging and loading, and no adjustment for a packing difference is posted without a second count.

title: Staging and loading
text:
1. Staging and loading take place only in Zone D under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Zone D is the 900 m2 dispatch area directly in front of outbound Doors 5-8. It holds only finished outbound loads that have been packed, labelled and wrapped. No picking, reserve storage, inbound inspection or quarantine activity takes place in Zone D.

2. Only wrapped, labelled pallets assigned to a specific door and load are staged in Zone D. Every pallet carries a readable system label with order, customer, quantity, pallet ID and destination, and has been wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Unlabelled, unwrapped or unassigned pallets, empty pallets and packing material are not staged in Zone D.

3. Staging is by door, load and departure sequence. The shift supervisor directs forklift operators to place pallets from packing to the marked staging lanes for Doors 5-8, clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and the 1.2 m segregated walkways behind yellow barriers. Loads are built in reverse loading order so the first drop is loaded last where applicable.

4. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg on every staged pallet. Placements are square, stable and scannable, labels outward. Any pallet showing collapse, leaning, wrap failure or damage at staging is removed immediately, recorded and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09, and is never loaded to make up quantity.

5. No truck is loaded without dispatcher release. The dispatcher books transport, assigns every carrier a specific outbound door from Doors 5-8 and a time slot, and releases each load from Zone D. Floor staff do not change doors, sequence or load composition, and drivers are not called from the marked waiting area until release is given.

6. Doors 5-8 are outbound only and open from Zone D. No inbound delivery is handled at an outbound door. A door is made ready before the vehicle is called: leveller confirmed operable, apron and walkway clear, staged pallets checked against the load list, and previous load cleared. No loading starts at a door whose leveller is tagged out of service.

7. Loading is carried out by forklift operators under supervisor direction. Drivers do not enter the hall and do not load. Drivers remain with the vehicle or as instructed at the dock edge under supervision while operators place pallets to the loading plan. Chocks and brakes are confirmed, the leveller is placed for the assigned vehicle only, and the 5 km/h regime at the dock ramps is observed.

8. Loading follows the dispatcher release and scanner control. Pallets are scanned from staging lane to trailer or van by the handheld WMS scanners to confirm pallet ID against the load. The 10 km/h limit applies inside, 15 km/h in the yard. Overloading, mixing of loads, or loading of hazmat, quarantine or held returns stock is not permitted.

9. Every loaded vehicle is checked and sealed before departure. The operator confirms count, stability and wrap intact, the supervisor or dispatcher confirms the load matches the release, doors are closed and the seal is applied and recorded by number. No unsealed or part-checked trailer or van leaves the dock apron.

10. Chilled loads are handled with minimum exposure. Goods from verified Zone E stock held between +2 C and +8 C are staged and loaded promptly, with Zone D doors kept closed except for the move. No expired, damaged or alarmed product is loaded, and any deviation holds the load until assessed under PR-12.

11. Every staging and loading operation is recorded for handover under PR-15. Door, slot, carrier, seal number, pallets staged versus loaded, re-wraps, quarantine moves and delays are entered in the shift log. Levellers are returned to stored position, doors closed and aprons cleared after each load, and unloaded or short loads roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until dispatcher release and sealing are complete.

title: Load and capacity limits
text:
1. Every load calculation on site is built on one fixed unit: a pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. No pallet exceeding this weight is packed, wrapped, staged in Zone D or loaded, and all trailer, van and per-shift capacities in this section assume full-weight 1,000 kg pallets.

2. The contracted curtain-side trailer is the standard outbound unit under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Each trailer carries at most 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions. Weight governs before floor space governs, so a trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets, even though floor positions remain physically free.

3. Trailers are loaded only to the WMS release and loading plan. Pallet IDs are scanned from the Zone D staging lane to the trailer, count and weight are reconciled against the 24,000 kg and 24-pallet limits, and no additional pallet, part-pallet or loose carton is added to make up floor positions once either limit is reached.

4. The delivery van is the small-drop unit only. Each van carries at most 1,200 kg on 6 floor positions. Weight again governs, so a van takes one full-weight 1,000 kg pallet only. Any consignment heavier than 1,200 kg, or requiring more than one full-weight pallet, goes by trailer and is not split across vans to avoid the limit.

5. Van loads are staged, scanned and sealed like trailer loads. Only wrapped, labelled pallets assigned to that van and door are staged in Zone D, placed square and stable with labels outward, and confirmed against the release before the doors are closed. Overloading the van axles or floor to use empty positions is not permitted.

6. Outbound throughput is limited by doors. Zone D serves 4 outbound doors, Doors 5-8, each handling at most 3 trailer loads per shift. This rate assumes levellers operable, staging lanes clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways, and forklift operators loading under supervisor direction with dispatcher release for each load.

7. The per-shift promise follows directly from doors and trailer capacity. At 4 doors times 3 trailer loads times 24 full-weight pallets, the most that can be promised to clients is 288 full-weight pallets per shift. This figure is fixed for planning, labour allocation and transport booking, and is not exceeded by adding pallets, overloading or staging at unassigned doors.

8. The 288-pallet figure is a maximum for conforming stock only. It counts only wrapped, labelled pallets released by the dispatcher from Zone D. Unlabelled, unwrapped, short, damaged, quarantine-held or hazmat pallets are never counted toward the shift total and are never loaded to reach it.

9. Dispatcher release enforces all limits. The dispatcher books transport to match the 3-loads-per-door rhythm, assigns each carrier a specific door from Doors 5-8 and a time slot, and releases each load only when pallet count, weight, destination and seal plan fit trailer or van limits. Floor staff do not change doors, add pallets or dispatch an overloaded vehicle.

10. Weight and balance are checked at loading. Operators confirm each pallet at or below 1,000 kg, distribute weight evenly in the trailer or van bed, secure against movement, and confirm wrap intact before sealing. Any pallet showing collapse, leaning or wrap failure is removed to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 and is not loaded.

11. Every load against these limits is recorded for handover under PR-15. Door, slot, carrier, trailer or van ID, pallet count, total weight against the 24,000 kg or 1,200 kg limit, seal number and any short or held pallets are entered in the shift log. Uncompleted loads roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00, and remain counted against the next shift's 288-pallet capacity when loaded.

title: MHE fleet
text:
1. The site operates an all-electric materials-handling fleet under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. No diesel or gas trucks are used in the hall. The fleet consists of 6 counterbalance forklifts, 4 reach trucks, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks, maintained as one pool and allocated daily by the shift supervisor.

2. The 6 counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t and are the general-work trucks. They handle unloading support at inbound Doors 1-4, transfer between Zones A to F, staging to Zone D, and loading at outbound Doors 5-8. They are not used for high-bay placement above the reach-truck levels in Zone B.

3. The 4 reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t and are the high-bay trucks for Zone B bulk storage. All put-away to and withdrawal from the high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 positions is performed with reach trucks, or with counterbalance trucks only where directed for aisle and height. Rack aisles are 3.0 m and are dimensioned for this operation.

4. The 8 electric pallet jacks are powered pedestrian or ride-on trucks for small and medium moves. They are used for Zone A bay clearance, replenishment support to Zone C, transfer of packed cartons to Zone D, and work in Zone E and Zone F where forklift movement is restricted by space or doors.

5. The 12 hand pallet jacks are non-powered and are used for short, light moves only. Pickers use them for small moves in Zone C, and packing staff use them at the packing benches and wrapper infeed. They are never used to move a pallet with load above 1,000 kg and never as a substitute for a powered truck on ramps.

6. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg on every truck. This limit is observed on all lifts, carries and placements, and governs the 2,700 kg per rack bay limit, the 4,000 kg hazmat cage limit, and the trailer and van limits. Any overweight or unstable pallet is secured, re-stacked and not moved until safe.

7. No licence, no truck. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators for counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks, personally and in writing. The shift supervisor assigns only authorised operators to powered trucks, and floaters drive powered trucks only if separately authorised.

8. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day. The check covers brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains, mast, guarding, seat belt, battery charge and visible damage. The morning shift completes the full written record; the afternoon shift re-confirms status at 14:00 handover and fully checks any truck newly brought into service.

9. Any truck found defective is stopped immediately and tagged out. The operator reports to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, the truck is marked do-not-use, and it is not returned to service until repair is logged and clearance is given. A door leveller, wrapper or scanner fault found during the check is tagged in the same way.

10. Charging, batteries and parking are controlled. Trucks are charged only in the designated charging points clear of walkways, dock aprons and the hazmat cage, with cables kept off the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers. Trucks are parked at shift end with forks lowered, brakes on, keys removed and levellers and aisles left clear.

11. Every fleet movement is recorded for handover under PR-15. Trucks checked, operators authorised, defects tagged, repairs logged by the maintenance technician, and trucks still out of service are entered in the shift log. Open defects and missing trucks roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared, and seat-belt use whenever the truck is moving is enforced on every shift.

title: Aisles and speed limits
text:
1. Internal movement runs on two fixed aisle widths inside the hall under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. These widths are minimum clear widths and are kept free at all times.

2. Main transport aisles of 4.0 m carry all inter-zone travel between Zones A to F and to the docks. Counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, reach trucks rated at 1.6 t in transit, and electric pallet jacks share these aisles. Pallets are carried low, loads do not overhang into opposite lanes, and staging, wrapping or inspection never takes place in the 4.0 m clearance.

3. Rack storage aisles of 3.0 m serve the high-bay pallet racking in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions. They are dimensioned for reach-truck operation for put-away and withdrawal. Only one truck works a rack aisle bay at a time, masts are raised and lowered only when stationary, and block stacking to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m never encroaches into the 3.0 m running clearance.

4. Pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from vehicle aisles by yellow barriers. The barrier line is fixed. Barriers are never removed, driven over, or used for leaning pallets, and the 1.2 m walkway is never used for truck travel, pallet staging, charging cables or waste.

5. Crossings, dock ramps and marked pedestrian zones are the only points where foot and truck routes meet. They are marked on the floor and kept visible. Pedestrians cross only at designated crossings, drivers stop and give way, and no pallet, wrapper film or equipment is left on a crossing or ramp apron.

6. Speed limits are simple and enforced by the shift supervisor. The limit is 10 km/h inside the building for all forklifts, reach trucks, electric pallet jacks and vans entering dock aprons. It applies in Zones A to F, in 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, with seat belts worn whenever the truck is moving.

7. The limit in the fenced yard of about 3,500 m2 is 15 km/h. It applies to all road vehicles in circulation and manoeuvring areas and to MHE crossing the yard. Approach to Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound, turning at the dock aprons and movement past the marked driver waiting area remain under this limit until the 5 km/h zone begins.

8. A limit of 5 km/h applies wherever people and trucks meet. This covers marked pedestrian zones, designated crossings, the 1.2 m walkway interfaces, and the dock ramps and leveller areas at all eight doors at 1.2 m dock height. Trucks slow to walking pace, sound the horn where marked, and stop if a pedestrian is on the crossing.
