9. Door aprons and ramp edges are controlled 5 km/h areas. Only the vehicle assigned to that live door and the staff handling that load are present during docking, leveller placement and loading or unloading. Other vehicles and pedestrians do not use or cross a live apron, and reversing is directed by a banksman clear of barriers.

10. Aisles, walkways and speed markings are checked each shift. The supervisor confirms 4.0 m aisles clear, 3.0 m rack aisles unobstructed, 1.2 m walkways behind intact yellow barriers, and crossing and 5 km/h markings legible. Any blocked aisle, damaged barrier or faded marking is reported to the maintenance technician, recorded in the shift log, and cleared before doors are released.

11. Every breach and obstruction is handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Speeding, barrier damage, blocked aisles or walkways, and apron incursions are recorded with truck, door and zone, reviewed as incidents, and carried forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory for everyone on the floor without exception.

title: Dock and packing equipment
text:
1. Dock and packing equipment is limited to three types on site: 8 dock levellers, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and 1 cardboard baler. All three run under PR-06 Outbound dispatch and PR-05 Packing and labelling for use, and under the maintenance regime for upkeep. No other fixed dock or packing plant is operated.

2. Each of the 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height has its own leveller. Doors 1-4 inbound serving Zone A and Doors 5-8 outbound serving Zone D each rely on their leveller for every loading and unloading operation. A door whose leveller is tagged out of service is not assigned by the dispatcher and no vehicle is docked there.

3. Levellers are placed only for the assigned vehicle. The operator confirms brakes and chocks, places the leveller square on the trailer or van bed, and observes the 5 km/h regime at the dock ramp. The lip must rest fully, the deck must sit level without bounce, and any jamming, distortion or hydraulic fault stops the operation immediately.

4. Levellers are returned to the stored position after each load. The deck is cleaned of wrap, strapping and debris, the control is left in park, and the door is closed before the dispatcher reassigns it. Leveller pits, edges and ramp aprons are kept clear of pallets, jacks and charging cables, and of the 1.2 m walkway line.

5. The 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers sit at the entry to Zone D dispatch and are run by dispatch and packing staff. Only wrapped, labelled pallets assigned to a specific door and load are staged past the wrappers. No unwrapped pallet is staged by Doors 5-8 and no unwrapped pallet is loaded.

6. Wrapping is to standard on every pallet with load up to 1,000 kg. Film is attached at the base, run base to top with sufficient turns to bind load to pallet, with corners and top layer secured and labels left readable and scannable. Loads failing wrap check for loose film, exposed corners or leaning are re-wrapped before staging.

7. The 1 cardboard baler stands clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways and takes only cardboard offcuts, backing and damaged cartons from packing. Plastic film, strapping, labels and general waste are segregated to bins and never fed to the baler. Bales are strapped, marked and stacked clear of dock aprons and fire exits.

8. Serviceability is confirmed each shift. The shift supervisor confirms both wrappers turntable, mast, film carriage and guarding operable, the baler emergency stop, guarding and bale chamber serviceable, and live door levellers operating and returning to stored position. Results are entered in the shift log under PR-15.

9. Any defect is tagged out immediately. The operator stops the leveller, wrapper or baler, reports to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and marks it do-not-use. Tagged equipment is not used, bypassed or reset by floor staff until repair is logged and clearance is given, and the affected door or lane is closed for planning.

10. The maintenance technician owns upkeep and logs every repair. Levellers, wrappers and the baler are maintained to maker schedule, with guards, interlocks, hydraulics, electrics and dock edge protection checked and recorded. Racking monthly inspection and evacuation quarterly drill do not replace this log, and no repair is closed without test run.

11. Every dock and packing equipment status is handed over. Levellers operable or tagged by door, wrappers and baler serviceable or out of service, re-wraps, bale changes and repairs logged or pending are entered in the shift log. Open tag-outs, missing film or blocked aprons roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared by the responsible owner.

title: Forklift operation
text:
1. All forklift and MHE operation runs under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. It covers the all-electric fleet: 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks. No other powered truck is used on site.

2. Counterbalance trucks are the general-work trucks for transfers between Zones A to F, unloading support at Doors 1-4 and loading at Doors 5-8. Reach trucks are the high-bay trucks for put-away and withdrawal in Zone B racking with 2,400 positions. Electric pallet jacks handle small and medium moves, and hand pallet jacks handle short, light moves only.

3. No licence, no truck. Only the warehouse manager authorises new forklift operators, personally and in writing, for counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks and electric pallet jacks. The company employs 8 forklift operators, and the shift supervisor assigns only authorised operators to powered trucks on each shift.

4. Authorisation is checked at shift start. The supervisor confirms names against the authorised list before allocating put-away, replenishment, staging and dock tasks. Floaters drive powered trucks only if separately authorised as forklift operators, and pickers and inbound operators do not drive unless so authorised.

5. Every powered truck receives a documented check before its first use each day. The operator checks brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains and mast, guarding, seat belt, battery charge and visible damage, and records the result. The morning shift completes the full record; the afternoon shift re-confirms status at 14:00 and fully checks any truck newly brought into service.

6. Any defect stops the truck immediately. The operator tags it do-not-use, reports to the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and it is not returned to service until repair is logged and clearance is given. A truck with faulty brakes, steering, horn, lights or seat belt is never used to finish a task.

7. Seat belts are worn whenever the truck is moving, with no exceptions. The belt is fastened before the key is turned, stays fastened during travel with forks low, and is checked as part of the daily check. Reach-truck and jack operators use the fitted restraint or stand-on protection as instructed.

8. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg on every lift. Operators confirm stable, wrapped pallets, carry low without overhang into opposite lanes, raise and lower masts only when stationary, and observe the 2,700 kg limit per rack bay in Zone B. Overweight, collapsed, leaning or leaking pallets are secured, reported and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

9. Speed limits are enforced by the shift supervisor. The limit is 10 km/h inside the building in all zones, in 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles. The limit is 15 km/h in the fenced yard of about 3,500 m2. The limit drops to 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet: marked pedestrian zones, designated crossings, 1.2 m walkway interfaces and dock ramps at all eight doors.

10. Aisles and separation are observed on every move. The 1.2 m pedestrian walkways behind yellow barriers are never driven on or staged in, crossings are used at walking pace with horn where marked, and drivers stop and give way to pedestrians. Dock aprons are entered only for the assigned live door, with chocks and brakes confirmed and leveller correctly placed.

11. Every authorisation, check and breach is recorded for handover under PR-15. Operators authorised, trucks checked, defects tagged, repairs logged and speeding or belt failures observed are entered in the shift log. Open tag-outs and unauthorised driving roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 as incidents reviewed by the supervisor until cleared.

title: Pedestrian safety
text:
1. Pedestrian safety runs under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. It applies to everyone on site — floor staff, supervisors, maintenance, visitors and drivers — wherever foot routes meet truck routes inside the 6,000 m2 hall and in the fenced yard of about 3,500 m2.

2. Foot and truck traffic are separated by construction. Pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide and are physically separated from vehicle aisles by yellow barriers. The barrier line is fixed. Barriers are never removed, driven over, climbed, or used for leaning pallets, wrap or equipment.

3. The 1.2 m walkways are for people only. They are never used for forklift, reach-truck or pallet-jack travel, for pallet staging, for charging cables, or for waste and packing material. Any pallet, jack or obstruction found on a walkway is removed immediately and reported to the shift supervisor.

4. Vehicle aisles are for trucks only. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide between Zones A to F and to the docks, and rack storage aisles in Zone B are 3.0 m wide. Pedestrians do not walk in vehicle aisles except to cross at a designated crossing, and never walk behind a manoeuvring truck or under raised forks.

5. Foot and truck routes meet only at marked points. Designated crossings, marked pedestrian zones, the 1.2 m walkway interfaces, and the dock ramps at all eight doors at 1.2 m dock height are marked on the floor and kept visible. Pedestrians cross only at designated crossings and drivers stop and give way.

6. A limit of 5 km/h applies wherever people and trucks meet. This covers marked pedestrian zones, designated crossings, walkway interfaces and dock ramps and leveller areas. Trucks slow to walking pace, sound the horn where marked, and stop if a pedestrian is on the crossing. The general limits remain 10 km/h inside and 15 km/h in the yard.

7. Dock aprons and door approaches are controlled areas. Only the vehicle assigned to that live door and the staff handling that load are present during docking, leveller placement and loading or unloading at Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound. Other pedestrians and vehicles do not use or cross a live apron.

8. Drivers are kept out of pedestrian-truck interfaces in the hall. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area in the yard until called to their door and time slot, stay with the vehicle or as instructed at the dock edge under supervision, and never enter the hall or wait in circulation lanes, at unassigned doors or on crossings.

9. Visibility and PPE are mandatory on every walkway and crossing. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are required for everyone on the warehouse floor, with no exceptions. In low light, at dock edges and in the yard after dark, pedestrians keep to lit walkways and make eye contact with the driver before stepping onto a crossing.

10. Walkways, barriers and markings are checked each shift. The shift supervisor confirms 1.2 m walkways clear and unobstructed, yellow barriers intact, crossings and 5 km/h markings legible, and dock ramp edges and aprons clear of pallets and film. Any blocked walkway, damaged barrier or faded marking is recorded, reported to the maintenance technician, and cleared before doors are released.

11. Every breach and obstruction is handed over under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Walking outside walkways, crossing outside crossings, barrier damage, blocked 4.0 m or 3.0 m aisles, apron incursions and 5 km/h violations are entered in the shift log with zone, door and names, reviewed by the supervisor as incidents, and carried forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared.

title: PPE
text:
1. Personal protective equipment on site runs under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. It is limited to three mandatory items for everyone on the floor, plus task-specific protection only where a procedure directs it. No work on the warehouse floor starts or continues without the mandatory items worn correctly.

2. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, with no exceptions. This covers floor staff, shift supervisors, the warehouse manager on the floor, maintenance, visitors and any driver called to the dock edge. The vest is worn fastened and visible over outer clothing at all times inside the 6,000 m2 hall, on dock ramps and in the yard interfaces.

3. Class S3 safety footwear is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, with no exceptions. Trainers, light shoes, open footwear and worn or split safety boots are not permitted in Zones A to F, on the 1.2 m walkways, at crossings or on dock aprons. Footwear is laced and intact, with toe cap, puncture plate and slip-resistant sole as per S3.

4. Seat belts are worn by forklift operators whenever the truck is moving, with no exceptions. The belt is fastened before the key is turned, stays fastened during travel with forks low in the 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, and is released only after the truck is parked with brakes on. Reach-truck and electric pallet-jack operators use the fitted restraint or stand-on protection as instructed.

5. Vests and footwear are checked at shift start by the shift supervisor. Staff without a serviceable vest or correct S3 footwear are not assigned to Zones A to F, to Doors 1-4 inbound or Doors 5-8 outbound, or to the yard walkways and crossings. Floaters, new starters and contractors are checked in the same way before entering the floor.

6. Seat belts are checked as part of the documented check before first use each day. The operator confirms belt webbing, buckle and retractor operable on each of the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, with restraint protection confirmed on the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t and 8 electric pallet jacks. A truck with a faulty belt or restraint is tagged out and reported to the supervisor and maintenance technician.

7. Drivers and visitors are covered by the same rule when they leave the marked waiting area or office annex. A driver called to the dock edge at 1.2 m dock height for checks under supervision wears vest and S3 footwear, stays as instructed, and never enters the hall without them. No spare vest or overshoe arrangement replaces the requirement.

8. Task-specific protection does not replace the mandatory items. Work in the 300 m2 Zone E cold store held between +2 °C and +8 °C uses warm clothing to instruction with vest still visible, and spill response in the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage uses only the dedicated spill kits and PPE to PR-13 instruction. Value-added packing in Zone F uses any cut, dust or handling protection stated in the work instruction in addition to vest and footwear.

9. PPE is kept serviceable by the wearer and the supervisor. Soiled, torn or faded vests that lose visibility, damaged footwear, and frayed or jammed belts are taken out of use immediately, reported, and replaced before the next task. Vests and boots are stored clean and dry, clear of the 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, dock aprons and the hazmat cage, and are never left on forks, barriers or racking.

10. Enforcement belongs to the shift supervisor on duty. Speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h where people and trucks meet do not reduce the PPE rule. Anyone found on the floor without vest or S3 footwear is stopped and removed from the floor, any driver without belt while moving is stopped, and the breach is recorded as an incident.

11. Every PPE check and breach is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Vests and footwear confirmed, belts checked with trucks, replacements issued, tag-outs for belt faults, and removals or warnings for non-compliance are entered in the shift log. Open replacements and unresolved breaches roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared by the responsible owner.

title: Cycle counts
text:
1. Cycle counts run every working day under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. They are the daily control that keeps system stock equal to rack stock across Zones A to F. Counting never stops for operations, and operations never block the count programme once it is released for the day.

2. The 2 stock controllers own the programme day to day. They set the rotating zone schedule, issue count tasks, direct recounts, investigate differences and prepare adjustments. The shift supervisor allocates time, aisles and scanner access, but does not change the count list or cancel a count once issued.

3. The schedule rotates to cover the whole hall. Each working day a defined part of Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone, Zone F cage and quarantine, and Zone A and Zone D staging checks is counted. High-movement and high-value lines are counted more often, and every location is counted at least once within the rotation.

4. Counts are issued as WMS tasks to the 20 handheld scanners. Counters scan the location label then each pallet ID, confirm item, quantity, batch and expiry where applicable, and enter the count on the scanner. Paper tallies, eye estimates and counting from memory are not permitted.

5. Counting is done by staff assigned by the shift supervisor, checked by the stock controllers. Counters work clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, with trucks held clear of the bay being counted. Zone E counts use minimum door-open time with the store held between +2 °C and +8 °C.

6. The first count is blind to system quantity. The counter does not see the book figure before entering the result. On posting, the system compares count to book. A match closes the location. Any difference locks the location as short, over or misplaced and triggers the recount rule below.

7. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Every difference goes to an independent recount directed by the stock controllers and carried out by a different counter from the first. The second counter recounts location, pallet ID, adjacent beams and pick face for misplacement before any figure is changed.

8. If the second count matches the first count, the difference is confirmed for investigation. Stock controllers check receipts in Zone A, put-away to Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, picks, packing and loading from Zone D, returns in Zone F and quarantine moves the same day. Misplaced pallets are moved by scan to correct location rather than adjusted.

9. If the second count matches the book figure, the first count is treated as miscount and no adjustment is made. If the two counts differ from each other and from book, a third check is directed by the stock controllers with the shift supervisor present, and the location remains system-blocked until resolved.

10. Controlled stock follows the same rule with no shortcut. Hazmat in the 60 m2 ventilated cage against the 4,000 kg limit, quarantine holds in Zone F, and chilled stock in Zone E are counted by assigned trained staff, with labels, closures and temperature discipline to PR-12 and PR-13. No return is restocked and no damaged-goods write-off is prepared to clear a count difference.

11. Every count day is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Locations counted, matches, differences, second counts pending, blocked locations and adjustments prepared are entered in the shift log. Recounts and blocked locations roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared, and any adjustment is prepared only after the second count and approved under the write-off thresholds.

title: Annual stocktake
text:
1. The annual stocktake is a full wall-to-wall count of all stock on site under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. It covers every pallet, carton and unit in Zones A to F, including Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, Zone C pick faces, Zone E cold zone, Zone F hazmat cage and quarantine, Zone A receipts and Zone D staging. No location is excluded or sampled.

2. The stocktake is held once a year and the site is shut down for it. No receiving at Doors 1-4, no put-away to Zone B, no replenishment to Zone C, no picking, packing or loading from Zone D takes place during the count window. The date is set by the warehouse manager and all client deliveries and dispatches are rescheduled around it.

3. Preparation is directed by the 2 stock controllers. Before shutdown they freeze open receipts in Zone A, confirm all booked put-away is stored by scan, clear Zone C transfer routes and Zone D lanes to identifiable pallets, segregate quarantine holds in Zone F, and confirm the hazmat cage quantity against its 4,000 kg limit. The 20 handheld WMS scanners are charged, tested and allocated to count teams.

4. Stock is frozen at cut-off. All WMS movements are stopped, open tasks are closed or parked, and the book position by location, pallet ID, batch and expiry is snapshoted. Any pallet moved after cut-off for safety or temperature reasons is moved only under supervisor direction and recorded by scan for reconciliation.

5. Counting is organised by zone teams under the shift supervisor present. Counters work in pairs by aisle and bay, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers. Each team counts location label then pallet ID, item, quantity, batch and expiry where applicable, entered on the scanner. Paper estimates and memory counts are not permitted.

6. All counts are blind to the book figure. The counter does not see system quantity before entering the result. The system compares count to book on posting. A match closes the location. Any difference locks the location and triggers an independent second count by a different counter, covering the location, adjacent beams and pick face for misplacement.

7. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. This rule applies in full at stocktake as on daily cycle counts. If second count matches first count, the difference is confirmed for investigation. If second count matches book, the first count is treated as miscount. If both differ, a third check is directed with the supervisor present and the location stays blocked.

8. Controlled stock is counted with its discipline intact. Zone E is counted with minimum door-open time, held between +2 °C and +8 °C with alarm cover and manual verification recorded. The 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage is counted by assigned trained staff without opening containers, against the 4,000 kg limit. Quarantine goods remain blocked and are counted but never used to clear a difference.

9. Reconciliation follows the count. Stock controllers investigate every confirmed difference against receipts, put-away, replenishment, picks, packing, loading, returns and quarantine moves, move misplaced pallets by scan to correct location, and prepare adjustments only after the second-count rule is met. Write-offs follow value approval: up to 500 EUR by the shift supervisor, above 500 EUR reserved to the manager.

10. The stocktake is closed only by the warehouse manager. The manager reviews locations counted, matches, confirmed differences, second and third counts, blocked locations and adjustments prepared, and signs off the results personally. No stocktake result is issued to clients and no post-stocktake adjustment is posted until that signature is recorded.

11. Every stocktake is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Cut-off time, teams and zones counted, scanner allocation, differences, recounts, blocked locations, Zone E readings, cage weight, quarantine holds, adjustments posted and the manager sign-off are entered in the shift log. Open blocks and pending approvals roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared, and normal operations restart only after sign-off.

title: Adjustments and racking
text:
1. No inventory figure is changed except by a formal adjustment under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. An adjustment is a system correction prepared by the 2 stock controllers after investigation, and it is the only way to bring book stock into line with physical stock. Direct editing of quantities at the scanner, in Zone A, Zone C or Zone D, is not permitted.

2. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Every difference found by cycle count or annual stocktake goes to an independent recount by a different counter, covering the location, adjacent beams and pick face for misplacement. If the second count matches book, no adjustment is made. If it confirms the first count, the difference is investigated before any adjustment is prepared.

3. Investigation comes before posting. Stock controllers check receipts in Zone A, put-away to Zone B, replenishment to Zone C, picks, packing and loading from Zone D, returns in Zone F and quarantine moves the same day. A misplaced pallet is moved by WMS scan to its correct location rather than adjusted, and open tasks, unbooked receipts and staged pallets are cleared from the enquiry first.

4. Controlled stock is never used to clear a difference. Hazmat in the 60 m2 ventilated cage against the 4,000 kg limit, goods blocked in quarantine in Zone F, and chilled stock in Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C are not adjusted across each other. No return is restocked and no damaged-goods write-off is prepared to force a count to match.

5. Adjustments that write off value follow fixed approval. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager. The threshold applies per incident or finding, and splitting one finding into smaller lines to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

6. Damaged-goods adjustments follow PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Goods moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day found remain system-blocked until disposition as restock, rework or scrap. Restock needs shift-supervisor disposition after inspection; scrap or write-off needs value approval under item 5 before the adjustment is posted.

7. Every adjustment is recorded and handed over. Location, pallet ID, item, batch and expiry, first and second counts, investigation result, value and approver are entered in the shift log under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Blocked locations stay blocked until the adjustment is approved and posted, and roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00.

8. Racking safety is inspected separately from counting under PR-08. The high-bay pallet racking in Zone B with 2,400 positions receives a documented safety inspection every month. The inspection covers uprights, beams, bracing, beam locks, base plates, bay load plates, upright protection and visible impact, twist or corrosion.

9. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg, and free block-stacking elsewhere is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. The monthly inspection confirms plates legible, no bay overloaded, no overhang or contact with uprights, and block stacks square, stable and clear of the 4.0 m main aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers.

10. Damage found at any time is tagged and taken out of use. The finder secures the bay, informs the shift supervisor and the maintenance technician, and the beam or bay is marked do-not-use. It is not loaded, counted as available capacity or offered for put-away or replenishment until logged repair and clearance. Findings from daily operation are added to the monthly record.

11. The maintenance technician owns racking repair and logs every repair. Monthly inspection results, tag-outs, impacts, overloads and clearances are recorded, reported to the warehouse manager, and carried in the handover until closed. An adjustment arising from damaged stock on a damaged bay is prepared only after the second-count rule is met and approved under the write-off thresholds above.

title: Returns handling
text:
1. Returns are handled only in Zone F under PR-07 Returns handling. The 600 m2 services and control area contains the dedicated returns inspection bays, physically separate from value-added packing, quarantine and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. No return is inspected, decided or restocked in Zone A, B, C, D or E.

2. Returns are accepted only within 14 days of delivery. The 4 returns and packing staff verify delivery date, customer, order reference, item, quantity and reason for return at receipt in Zone F. Any unit outside the 14-day window, without traceable delivery reference, or arriving as unannounced hazmat or chilled goods without paperwork is held, recorded and escalated to the shift supervisor and dispatcher.

3. Returns arriving at inbound Doors 1-4 are not treated as inbound receipts. Identified at document check in Zone A, they are transferred promptly to Zone F without booking as stock, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers. They remain system-blocked until inspection and disposition are complete.

4. Every unit is inspected, without sampling. Returns staff open, count and check each carton and unit for condition, cleanliness, seal integrity, labelling, batch and expiry where applicable, and for chilled lines transport condition. Inspection results are recorded by line on the returns record with date, origin and inspector initials.

5. Damaged, suspect or non-conforming units found during inspection are segregated immediately. Anything wet, open, expired, mislabelled, leaking or showing temperature abuse is marked, recorded and moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day it is found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. It is never placed with conforming returns awaiting decision.

6. After inspection, returns staff propose disposition by line: restock, rework or scrap. Restock is proposed only for sealed, clean, in-date, correctly labelled units fit for Zone B, Zone C or Zone E. Rework is proposed for units that can be made conforming by defined packing work in Zone F. All else is proposed as scrap.

7. Nothing is restocked, reworked or scrapped without approval. Only the shift supervisor decides final disposition as restock, rework or scrap on proposal from returns staff. No return is moved to bulk storage, pick faces or the cold zone, and no WMS adjustment is posted, before that decision is recorded.

8. Restock is by scan to defined location. Approved units are correctly labelled, scanned from Zone F to the WMS-directed location in Zone B, chilled Zone E stock held between +2 °C and +8 °C, or Zone C face only via replenishment, with batch and expiry confirmed. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Unlabelled or unapproved units are never restocked.

9. Rework is carried out only in Zone F to instruction. Approved units are re-packed, re-labelled or re-wrapped as directed, re-inspected unit by unit, and only then presented again for supervisor disposition. Reworked units that fail second inspection go to quarantine as scrap. Hazmat returns are never reworked outside PR-13 instruction.

10. Scrap and value loss follow fixed approval. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR; any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count directed by the 2 stock controllers, and splitting one finding to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

11. Every return is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Receipt date, 14-day check, quantities received, inspected, restocked, reworked and scrapped, quarantine moves, second counts pending and approvals are entered in the shift log. Open inspections, rework in progress and blocked quarantine holds roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until disposition and posting are complete.

title: Damaged goods
text:
1. Damaged goods are handled only under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Any pallet, carton or unit found collapsed, leaning, wet, open, crushed, leaking, mislabelled, expired or otherwise unfit is treated as damaged from the moment it is found, wherever it is found in Zones A to F, in the yard or at the docks.

2. Discovery stops that line. The finder does not put away, pick, pack or load the goods, does not mix them with conforming stock, and does not attempt repair on the spot. The pallet is secured where found clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles, 3.0 m rack aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, and the shift supervisor is informed immediately.

3. Damaged goods go to quarantine the same day they are found. Transfer to quarantine in Zone F services and control is completed before end of shift, without overnight hold in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C or Zone D. The 4 returns and packing staff or assigned forklift operator moves the goods under supervisor direction, with a pallet with load at most 1,000 kg, intact where possible or re-stacked for safe movement.

4. Quarantine in Zone F is physically separate from value-added packing, returns inspection and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. Damaged hazmat is segregated to PR-13 instruction and never placed with general quarantine unless the cage procedure directs it. Conforming reserve, pick or dispatch stock is never placed in quarantine.

5. Every quarantine arrival is labelled and blocked. The label shows date found, origin zone and door, receipt or order reference, item and quantity, reason for hold, and finder initials. The WMS location is set to quarantine blocked status on the handheld scanners, so the stock cannot be offered for replenishment, picking or loading.

6. Inspection follows segregation. Returns and packing staff inspect each unit for condition, count, labelling, batch and expiry where applicable, and for chilled lines temperature evidence for Zone E stock held between +2 C and +8 C. Results are recorded by line, and leaking, odorous or hazardous units are handled only with dedicated spill kits and PPE to PR-13.

7. After inspection, staff propose disposition: restock, rework or scrap. Restock is proposed only for fully conforming units; rework only where defined packing work in Zone F can make the unit conforming; all else as scrap. Only the shift supervisor decides final disposition, and no unit leaves quarantine without that recorded decision.

8. Value loss follows fixed write-off approval. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to and including 500 EUR. Any write-off above 500 EUR is reserved to the warehouse manager. The threshold applies per incident or finding, and splitting one finding into smaller lines to stay below the threshold is not permitted.

9. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. Every quarantine difference goes to an independent recount directed by the 2 stock controllers, covering the quarantine location and the origin beam or face for misplacement. Misplaced pallets are moved by scan to correct location rather than adjusted, and no return is restocked to clear a damaged-goods difference.

10. The area and cause are made safe together with the goods. Racking impact, wrapper failure, spill or temperature deviation behind the damage is tagged out, reported to the maintenance technician, and recorded as an incident for supervisor review before close of shift. The beam, wrapper, leveller or scanner stays out of use until logged repair and clearance.

11. Every damaged-goods case is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Date, zone, pallet IDs, quantities quarantined, restocked, reworked and scrapped, second counts pending, value and approver, and tag-outs are entered in the shift log. Open quarantine holds and pending approvals above 500 EUR roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until disposition and posting are complete.

title: Value-added packing
text:
1. Value-added packing is carried out only in Zone F under instruction. The 600 m2 services and control area contains the defined packing benches, physically separate from returns inspection bays, quarantine and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. No value-added or rework packing takes place in Zone A, Zone B, Zone C or Zone D.

2. Only approved work is packed. The 4 returns and packing staff work solely to a written instruction and to supervisor disposition: approved rework of returns or damaged goods as rework, or defined client packing such as sets, displays and relabelling. Goods blocked in quarantine, goods awaiting inspection, and hazmat outside PR-13 instruction are never packed as conforming product.

3. Rework follows inspection and proposal. Units proposed as rework after returns inspection in Zone F are held segregated until the shift supervisor decides final disposition as restock, rework or scrap. Only units with recorded rework approval are brought to the bench, by quantity and line, clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers.

4. Packing is to instruction, scan-checked where directed. Packers confirm item, quantity, batch and expiry where applicable on the 20 handheld WMS scanners, use the specified carton, fill and seal, and separate orders and customers. Mixing of batches, expiry dates or customers in one unit without system direction is not permitted.

5. Every reworked and value-added unit is labelled before release. Labels show item, quantity, batch and expiry, pallet ID where palletised, and order reference where applicable, applied flat, readable and scannable. Units without a readable label remain at the bench and are never moved to Zone B, Zone C, Zone E or Zone D.

6. Reworked units are re-inspected unit by unit. After packing, returns and packing staff re-count and re-check condition, seal integrity, labelling and cleanliness, and present the result again for supervisor disposition. Units passing second inspection go to restock by scan; units failing go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 as scrap.

7. Restock from packing is by scan to defined location only. Approved units are scanned from Zone F to the WMS-directed location in Zone B bulk storage with 2,400 positions, to verified Zone E stock held between +2 °C and +8 °C for chilled lines, or to Zone C only via replenishment under PR-03. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg.

8. Chilled and hazmat lines follow controlled routing. Chilled rework is packed with minimum ambient exposure and moved promptly to verified cold locations. Hazmat is never reworked outside PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response instruction, containers are never opened except as that procedure directs, and the 4,000 kg cage limit, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets, is never used to stage rework.

9. Damage found at the bench is segregated immediately. Damaged, wet, open, expired, mislabelled or leaking units are marked, recorded and moved to quarantine the same day, set to blocked status so they cannot be offered for replenishment or loading. Value loss follows fixed approval: up to and including 500 EUR by the shift supervisor, above 500 EUR reserved to the warehouse manager.

10. Packing waste is cleared at source. Cardboard offcuts, backing and damaged cartons go directly to the 1 cardboard baler, plastic film, strapping and labels are segregated to bins and never fed to the baler, and bales are strapped and stacked clear of aisles, walkways, dock aprons and fire exits. Benches, wrappers infeed and transfer routes are left clear with empty pallets returned to defined stacks.

11. Every packing run is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Instruction reference, quantities received for rework, packed, re-inspected, restocked and scrapped, label runs, baler changes, quarantine moves and second counts pending are entered in the shift log. Open rework, blocked holds and pending approvals roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count directed by the 2 stock controllers.

title: Cold-chain handling
text:
1. Cold-chain handling runs under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and covers all chilled goods on site. It applies from arrival at Doors 1-4 through Zone A inspection, put-away to Zone E, storage, replenishment to Zone C, picking, packing and loading from Zone D, including returns.

2. Zone E is the 300 m2 enclosed chilled store and the only place chilled stock is held. It is held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C with temperature alarms fitted. No ambient, hazmat, quarantine or returns stock is stored in Zone E, and no chilled stock is stored in Zone A, B, C, D or F outside controlled transfer.

3. Only booked goods enter Zone E. Goods remain in Zone A until documents, count, condition and transport temperature evidence have been checked under PR-01. Only inspected goods are booked into the WMS, and only booked, labelled pallets are released for put-away under PR-02. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg.

4. Transfer to and from Zone E is prompt. Chilled pallets move without delay clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, with Zone E doors closed immediately after each move. Booked pallets waiting for cold space wait secured in Zone A and are carried in the shift log.

5. The enclosure is kept closed and intact. Doors, seals, curtains and refrigeration are checked each shift, doors are opened only for put-away, replenishment, count or inspection, and exposure in ambient areas is limited to immediate transfer. Chilled pallets are never staged in ambient zones.

6. Temperature is verified manually each shift. The shift supervisor or assigned operator reads the independent thermometer, confirms +2 °C to +8 °C, checks the alarm panel for active or silenced alarms, and records time, reading and initials. Morning and afternoon shifts each record their own verification under PR-15.

7. Any deviation or alarm stops chilled flow. On out-of-range reading, alarm, door or refrigeration failure, stock is held in place, no further put-away, replenishment or picking of chilled lines takes place, and the shift supervisor takes charge. The warehouse manager is notified without delay.

8. Held product is not released until assessed under PR-12. Stock controllers and the supervisor check duration, temperature evidence and condition by batch and expiry, segregate suspect units and move them to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09. Conforming release and any scrap follow recorded disposition and value approval.

9. Chilled replenishment and picking draw only from verified stock. Pick faces for chilled lines are fed under PR-03 from Zone E held between +2 °C and +8 °C, and orders are picked in Zone C under PR-04 with minimum ambient exposure. No expired, damaged, alarmed or held product is issued or packed as conforming.

10. Inventory and returns in the cold chain follow the same accuracy rules. Cycle counts on the rotating schedule use minimum door-open time, no adjustment is ever posted without a second count directed by the 2 stock controllers, and returns are restocked to Zone E only after inspection in Zone F and shift-supervisor disposition as restock.

11. Every cold-chain check and movement is recorded for handover. Receipt numbers, pallet IDs, locations, temperature readings, alarm tests, holds, quarantine moves and WMS scans on the 20 handheld scanners are entered in the shift log. Open alarms, held stock and unresolved deviations remain named to an owner and roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared.

title: Hazmat handling
text:
1. Hazmat handling runs under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and covers all hazardous goods on site. It applies from arrival at Doors 1-4 through Zone A inspection, put-away to Zone F, storage, issue and spill response. No hazmat activity takes place outside this procedure.

2. The separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F services and control is the only place hazmat is held. Hazmat is never stored in Zone A, B, C, D or E, in walkways, on dock aprons, in the yard or in general quarantine. Any hazmat pallet found outside the cage is secured, reported as an incident and moved immediately under supervisor direction.

3. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at any time, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets. A pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg. Before any booked receipt is released from Zone A, the shift supervisor confirms remaining capacity by weight and pallet positions. If capacity is unavailable, booked pallets wait secured in Zone A and are carried in the shift log.

4. The cage is enclosed, lockable, ventilated and marked. Ventilation runs continuously, containers are kept closed, upright, sealed and labelled, and incompatible products are segregated to instruction. Containers are never opened except as PR-13 directs. Smoking, charging, hot work and decanting are prohibited at the cage.

5. Access is limited to trained staff assigned by the shift supervisor. Only operators authorised by the warehouse manager drive powered trucks for hazmat moves. Moves use intact pallets and wrap, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers, with 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings and dock ramps.

6. Put-away to the cage runs under PR-02 and PR-13. Only booked, labelled hazmat inspected in Zone A without opening containers is moved, by WMS scan of pallet and cage location on the handheld scanners. Labels, closures and integrity are confirmed at Zone A and at the cage. Leaking, odorous or unlabelled units are not racked but segregated as quarantine to PR-13 instruction.

7. The cage is checked visually each shift. The supervisor confirms quantity against the 4,000 kg limit, segregation and labelling intact, ventilation running, doors locked, spill kits present, complete and unused, and no product outside the 60 m2 boundary. Quantities and kit status are entered in the shift log under PR-15.

8. Spill response starts with making safe. On leakage, odour, damaged container or spill, the finder keeps clear, warns others, removes ignition sources, and informs the shift supervisor, who takes charge. The area is secured clear of aisles and walkways, people are kept upwind, and the warehouse manager is notified without delay.

9. Cleanup uses only the dedicated spill kits and PPE to PR-13 instruction. Absorbents, gloves, goggles and disposal bags from the cage station are used as directed, contaminated material is bagged, labelled and treated as quarantine blocked stock, and general packing material, baler waste and floor drains are never used. Used kits are reported for immediate replacement.

10. Nothing leaves the cage or spill quarantine without approval. Returns staff inspect and propose restock, rework or scrap, and only the shift supervisor decides final disposition. Write-offs up to and including 500 EUR are approved by the supervisor; above 500 EUR reserved to the warehouse manager. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count directed by the 2 stock controllers.

11. Every hazmat movement, check and spill is recorded for handover. Receipt numbers, pallet IDs, weights against the 4,000 kg limit, cage checks, spill events, kit use, quarantine labels, second counts and approvals are entered in the shift log. Open holds, over-limit risks and uncleared spills remain named to an owner and roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until logged repair and clearance.

title: Emergency evacuation
text:
1. Emergency evacuation runs under PR-14 Emergency evacuation and covers everyone on site. It applies inside the 6,000 m2 hall across Zones A to F, in the office annex, in the fenced yard of about 3,500 m2, and at all eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height, on both shifts and on approved Saturday overtime.

2. The shift supervisor on duty takes charge of every evacuation. On alarm, injury, fire, spill, gas, refrigeration failure or structural damage, the supervisor stops work, orders evacuation, secures the area so far as safe, accounts for staff, and notifies the warehouse manager without delay. No other role overrides the evacuation order.

3. Alarm means leave immediately. On hearing the fire alarm or the supervisor order, all forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks are stopped with forks lowered and brakes on where safe, wrappers and baler are left, Zone E doors and hazmat cage are left closed but not locked for escape, and all staff move on foot to the nearest marked escape route.

4. Escape routes use the separated pedestrian system. Staff leave by the 1.2 m walkways behind yellow barriers and designated crossings to the nearest fire exit, clear of the 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles where trucks may still be stopping. Pallets, jacks, wrap and equipment are never left on walkways, crossings or exit paths.

5. Drivers, visitors and contractors evacuate with the site. Drivers leave vehicles in the yard or at Doors 1-4 inbound and Doors 5-8 outbound with engines off, leave the dock apron clear, and join staff on foot. Drivers do not enter the hall to move a vehicle and do not wait in circulation lanes. Office staff leave the annex by its escape route.

6. The assembly point is by the north fence in the yard. All evacuees move directly there, keep clear of dock manoeuvring areas, trailer movements and the 5 km/h dock ramps, and remain at the point. High-visibility vests stay on. Leaving the assembly point for vehicles, lockers or the hall is not permitted.

7. Roll call is taken at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building. The supervisor checks names against the shift roster, the handover log, floaters, maintenance, dispatch, drivers signed in at the waiting area, and visitors. Missing persons are reported immediately to the emergency services and the warehouse manager. No search is made inside by staff.

8. Re-entry is controlled and happens only after roll call is complete and the all-clear is given. The supervisor confirms all persons accounted for, confirms with the emergency services or the warehouse manager that the building is safe, and only then releases staff by zone and door. No one re-enters before roll call and clearance, even for personal items or trucks.

9. After re-entry, the supervisor makes the site safe before restart. Zones A to F are walked for damage, blocked 4.0 m and 3.0 m aisles, displaced barriers, rack impact, leveller, wrapper and scanner faults, Zone E temperature between +2 °C and +8 °C, and hazmat cage 60 m2 integrity against the 4,000 kg limit. Unsafe plant is tagged out until logged repair.

10. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14. The date is set by the warehouse manager to cover both 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts across the year. The drill tests alarm, escape by walkways and exits, movement to the north fence, roll call and controlled re-entry, with observers timing each stage and noting blocked routes or missing names.

11. Every alarm, evacuation and drill is recorded for handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Time, cause, zones and doors affected, roll-call result, injuries or damage, tag-outs, Zone E readings and cage checks, and drill timings and corrective actions are entered in the shift log. The supervisor reviews every incident report before close of shift, and open actions roll forward at 14:00 and 22:00 until cleared.

title: Operator Authorisation and Daily Checks
text:
1. Only authorised forklift operators may operate powered materials handling equipment on site. Powered equipment means the 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, and the 8 electric pallet jacks. No licence, no truck.

2. Authorisation is personal and equipment-specific. An operator authorised only for electric pallet jacks may not drive a counterbalance forklift or a reach truck until separately trained, assessed and authorised for that truck type. The 12 hand pallet jacks for small moves may be used by other trained warehouse staff for manual moves in Zones A, C and D, but never for high-bay work or for riding.

3. New forklift operators are authorised only by the warehouse manager. A valid external licence or certificate alone is not sufficient. The warehouse manager verifies the licence, arranges site familiarisation covering Zones A to F, dock levellers, rack aisles, pedestrian walkways and the yard, and records a written authorisation before the operator works unsupervised. The list of authorised operators is kept current and available to both shift supervisors.

4. Authorisation may be suspended at any time. The warehouse manager or the shift supervisor in charge of the shift must stand down any operator who is involved in an incident, observed driving unsafely, or reported unfit for duty. Re-authorisation requires re-assessment by the warehouse manager. There are no exceptions in peak season or Saturday overtime.

5. Every powered truck must receive a documented pre-use check before its first use each day, as required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. The operator assigned to first use that truck on that shift completes the check using the standard checklist and signs it. A truck that has not passed and recorded its daily check must not be used, even for a short move.

6. The daily check covers the complete working condition of the truck. It includes brakes, steering, horn, lights and beacon, seat belt function on forklifts and reach trucks, forks and mast chains, hydraulic leaks, tyre condition, battery charge and cable condition, emergency stop and deadman functions on electric pallet jacks, and legibility of the rated capacity plate. Any damage to racking, dock equipment or barriers noticed during the check must also be reported.

7. If any safety-critical defect is found, the operator must tag the truck as out of service, remove the key where fitted, park it clear of transport aisles and dock doors, and inform the shift supervisor immediately. The shift supervisor ensures the defect is reported to the maintenance technician the same shift. Only the maintenance technician may release a truck back into service, and every repair is logged.

8. Checks and authorisations are traceable. Completed daily check sheets are handed to the shift supervisor at the end of the shift and retained for audit. Trucks shared between the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts do not need a second full documented check unless a new defect is suspected, but the incoming operator must walk around the truck and confirm the earlier record before driving.

title: Speed Limits and Driving Rules
text:
1. Speed limits apply to every powered truck on site and to every visiting vehicle moving in the yard. They are absolute maximums, not target speeds. The operator must always drive slower than the limit when visibility, load, floor conditions or pedestrian activity require it, as set out in PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

2. Inside the building the limit is 10 km/h. This covers the entire 6,000 m2 hall, including Zones A to F, the 4.0 m wide main transport aisles and the 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles in Zone B. No overtaking is permitted inside the building.

3. In the fenced yard of 3,500 m2 the limit is 15 km/h. This applies to our forklifts and pallet jacks when working outside, to the maintenance technician's service movements, and to all contracted trailers and delivery vans moving to and from the 8 dock doors.

4. Wherever people and trucks meet, the limit is 5 km/h walking pace. This means all marked pedestrian zones and crossings, the physically separated 1.2 m wide walkways wherever trucks cross them, and the dock ramps and leveller areas at all 8 doors. At crossings the truck must be prepared to stop completely.

5. Pedestrians always have priority. At pedestrian crossings, at the entrances to Zone C picking areas and Zone D staging areas, and at the marked waiting area where drivers wait for their door and time slot, the operator must stop and allow people to pass. Sounding the horn does not give priority; it is only a warning signal.

6. Additional driving rules protect stability and visibility. The operator must wear the seat belt whenever a counterbalance forklift or reach truck is moving, drive with the forks lowered to approximately 100-150 mm above the floor, never carry a pallet load above 1,000 kg, and never raise or lower a load while the truck is moving. The load must face uphill on the dock ramps and must never obstruct forward view — if it does, the operator must drive in reverse with a clear view in the direction of travel or use a banksman.

7. Aisle discipline is mandatory. Trucks keep to the right in the 4.0 m main transport aisles, keep within the marked lanes, and sound the horn before entering intersections, blind corners and the entries to Zones A and D. In the 3.0 m rack storage aisles in Zone B only one truck works in the aisle at a time; the second truck waits clear of the aisle entrance. Parking is permitted only in marked areas, never in front of dock doors, fire exits, the hazmat cage in Zone F, or the pedestrian barriers.

8. Dock work follows dispatcher control. No truck approaches doors 1-4 inbound or doors 5-8 outbound unless the trailer is correctly docked, braked, chocked and its leveller is confirmed in place by the inbound operator or dispatcher. Forklifts never enter a trailer that has not been released for loading or unloading, never drive beyond the marked dock edge without a fitted leveller, and never leave a dock door with the leveller raised.

9. Drivers of visiting lorries and vans never enter the hall and never drive beyond their assigned door and time slot. Yard movements are directed by the dispatcher and the shift supervisor in charge. Any breach of the 15 km/h yard limit or the 5 km/h limit at ramps and crossings is reported immediately to the shift supervisor and the dispatcher is informed to hold the carrier's slot.

10. Breaches by our own staff are treated as safety incidents. Exceeding a speed limit, failing to give way to pedestrians, driving with an unsecured or overweight load, or moving a truck without a seat belt is reported under the incident procedure and may lead to immediate suspension of authorisation under hs.ch01.s1. Both shift supervisors enforce these rules identically on the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and during any Saturday morning overtime.

title: Pedestrian Walkways and Conduct
text:
1. All pedestrian movement inside the 6,000 m2 hall and across the 3,500 m2 yard must use the designated pedestrian system required by PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. The system is segregated: people and powered trucks do not share the same traffic space except at marked crossings. Shortcuts through storage, staging or dock manoeuvring areas are prohibited.

2. Pedestrian walkways inside the building are physically separated from truck lanes by yellow barriers and are 1.2 m wide along their full length. The barriers must never be moved, climbed over, or used for leaning pallets, wrap, cages or hand pallet jacks against. Any damage to a barrier, missing section or blocked walkway must be reported to the shift supervisor immediately and cleared the same shift.

3. The walkways connect the office annex, welfare facilities, the entrances to Zones A to F, and the yard access doors. They run beside, not inside, the 4.0 m wide main transport aisles and do not enter the 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles in Zone B. Pedestrians must not walk down the centre of transport aisles or between racking where reach trucks and counterbalance forklifts are operating.

4. Every crossing of a truck lane is marked on the floor and, where needed, signed. Pedestrians may cross transport aisles, dock approaches and yard routes only at these marked crossings. Before stepping out, stop at the edge, look both ways, and make eye contact with any approaching operator. Never assume a truck will stop — even though the limit at all crossings is 5 km/h walking pace and pedestrians have priority, a laden truck needs distance to stop.

5. In Zone C picking and Zone D dispatch, where pickers, inbound operators and forklifts work close together, pedestrians must stay inside the marked lanes within the zone, keep to the right on two-way walkways, and never step out from behind pallets, flow racks, stretch wrappers or staged loads into a truck lane. When guiding or checking a load, stand clear of the mast swing and fork travel and remain visible to the operator at all times.

6. Dock areas are controlled areas. Pedestrians must not enter the dock ramps, leveller zones or trailer beds at doors 1-8 unless their task requires it and the dispatcher or shift supervisor has confirmed the trailer is braked, chocked and released. Never walk behind a reversing trailer, never cross between a docked trailer and the dock edge, and never enter a trailer while a forklift is working inside it. The dock edge is always kept clear.

7. Visiting drivers do not enter the hall as pedestrians. After docking at their assigned door and time slot under Doors 1-4 inbound only and Doors 5-8 outbound only, they wait in the marked waiting area until called. Warehouse staff must not invite drivers onto the floor and must escort any authorised visitor via the walkways in high-visibility vest and safety footwear.

8. Expected conduct on foot is simple: walk, do not run; do not wear headphones or hooded clothing that blocks sight or hearing; keep mobile phone use to stopped positions clear of lanes, with the 20 handheld WMS scanners operated only when standing clear; carry nothing that blocks forward view; and maintain at least 3 m clearance from a moving truck and from a raised load. At intersections and blind corners, use the convex mirrors and pause before proceeding.

9. Good housekeeping is part of pedestrian safety. Stretch film, strapping, spillages, loose cardboard from the baler area and trailing charging cables for electric pallet jacks must not be left on walkways or crossings. Anyone who sees an obstruction, slippery patch or failed light on a pedestrian route must make it safe if possible and report it to the shift supervisor for the maintenance technician to log and repair.

10. Both shift supervisors enforce the same standard on the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and on any Saturday morning overtime. Leaving a protected walkway, crossing outside a marked crossing, entering a dock or rack aisle against the rules, or moving or blocking a yellow barrier is treated as a safety incident and reported under the incident procedure. New starters learn Zones A to F walkways and crossings on day one before working unsupervised.

title: Mandatory PPE
text:
1. High-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, with no exceptions. The warehouse floor means the entire 6,000 m2 hall covering Zones A to F, including receiving, bulk storage, picking, dispatch, the cold zone and services, plus the dock ramps, leveller areas and yard routes where trucks and trailers move.

2. This rule applies equally to all people on site. It covers the warehouse manager, both shift supervisors, forklift operators, inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns and packing staff, the maintenance technician, dispatchers and floaters, on both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and on any Saturday morning overtime. Authorised visitors and contractors are included, and visiting drivers, who normally wait in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall, must also wear vest and safety footwear if exceptionally authorised to enter a controlled area.

3. High-visibility vests must be fastened and visible at all times on the floor. They must not be covered by coats, tabards or backpacks, removed for comfort, or replaced by non-approved garments. In the cold zone between +2 °C and +8 °C, thermal clothing is worn underneath the vest, never instead of it. Spare vests are available from the shift supervisor for visitors and for replacement of damaged or heavily soiled vests.

4. Safety footwear must be of class S3 as a minimum. That means closed footwear with protective toecap, puncture-resistant sole, closed and waterproof upper, cleated outsole and antistatic properties, suitable for dock levellers, rack aisles, cold and wet surfaces and yard work. Trainers, low cut shoes, sandals, wellingtons without toecap, or any footwear below S3 are prohibited on the floor, even for a short visit to Zones A to F or the office-to-hall threshold.

5. Footwear must be worn correctly laced or fastened, kept clean and inspected by the wearer. Any split upper, detached sole, damaged toecap or worn tread that reduces slip resistance must be reported to the shift supervisor the same shift and the pair replaced before the next entry to the floor. No one with unsuitable or damaged footwear may start or continue work in the hall or yard.

6. Forklift operators must wear the seat belt whenever a counterbalance forklift or reach truck is moving, as required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. This applies to all 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and all 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, laden or unladen, indoors in the 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles, on the dock ramps at doors 1-8, and outside in the 3,500 m2 yard. The belt is fastened before moving off and remains fastened until the truck is fully parked with parking brake applied.

7. The seat belt is part of the documented daily check. If the belt is missing, frayed, will not latch or retract, or the warning device where fitted is faulty, the truck is treated as having a safety-critical defect. The operator tags it out of service, parks it clear of aisles and doors, and reports it to the shift supervisor for the maintenance technician to log and repair. Only the maintenance technician may release the truck back into service.

8. Electric pallet jacks and hand pallet jacks have no seat belt, and this does not exempt safe operation. Operators of the 8 electric pallet jacks must use the deadman and emergency stop functions, walk alongside and never ride, and keep feet clear of the load and wheels in S3 footwear. The 12 hand pallet jacks may be used only by trained staff for small manual moves in Zones A, C and D.

9. Enforcement is identical on every shift. The shift supervisor in charge of the floor stops any person without correct vest or S3 footwear from entering or remaining on the floor, and stands down any operator moving a truck without a seat belt. Non-compliance is reported as a safety incident, may lead to suspension of forklift authorisation under hs.ch01.s1, and repeated breach is referred to the warehouse manager. New starters are issued PPE and instructed in Zones A to F requirements on day one before working unsupervised.

title: Cold Zone Rules
text:
1. Zone E is the only chilled storage area on site. It is a 300 m2 enclosed zone within the 6,000 m2 hall, held continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. No other zone is temperature-controlled, and no chilled goods may be stored outside Zone E.

2. The temperature range applies at all times, on both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts, on Saturday morning overtime, and overnight and at weekends when the hall is unoccupied. Doors, curtains and seals to Zone E must be kept closed except for the immediate movement of goods or trucks in and out. They must never be wedged open, and any damaged seal, curtain or door closer must be reported to the shift supervisor the same shift.

3. Temperature is monitored by automatic alarms and by manual verification each shift. The alarm system alerts to any excursion below +2 °C or above +8 °C. The manual verification is a recorded thermometer check carried out once per shift by the designated operator or stock controller, using the calibrated thermometer for Zone E. The result, time and name are entered in the cold-zone log and reviewed by the shift supervisor in charge.

4. If the alarm sounds or the manual check shows an out-of-range reading, work continues only to protect stock. The shift supervisor must be informed immediately, the doors kept closed, and no new chilled inbound put-away made into Zone E until the condition is confirmed. The shift supervisor informs the warehouse manager and calls the maintenance technician to inspect the refrigeration and alarm system the same shift, and every action and repair is logged.

5. Goods handling in Zone E follows the normal flow with cold-chain priority. Only booked chilled goods go to put-away in Zone E, replenishment of chilled pick faces is from Zone E stock, and chilled pallets never wait in ambient Zones A to D longer than needed for loading, picking or dispatch. Pallet loads remain subject to the 1,000 kg maximum, and cold or wet wrapping and labels are checked before pallets move to Zone D.

6. Personal protection in the cold zone builds on the site PPE rule. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear remain mandatory with no exceptions, and thermal clothing, hat and gloves are worn underneath the vest, never instead of it. Clothing must be dry, clean and close-fitting so it cannot catch in racking, flow racks, pallet jacks or the stretch wrappers. Spare thermal kit and vests are available from the shift supervisor.

7. Safe working in cold conditions requires common-sense rotation. Staff who feel numbness, excessive shivering, loss of concentration or slippery grip must leave Zone E immediately, warm up, and report to the shift supervisor, who rearranges the task or rotates staff. No one works alone for extended periods inside Zone E with the doors closed, and handheld WMS scanners must be operated only when standing clear of truck lanes.

8. Floor and equipment risks are higher in the cold and damp. The 10 km/h indoor limit and the 5 km/h limit where people and trucks meet apply fully in and around Zone E. Operators must allow longer braking distances on cold or condensing floors, keep forks at 100-150 mm, keep the dock-style evaporators, fans and sensors clear of pallets and wrap, and immediately report and make safe any water, ice or spillage. Pedestrians use only the marked 1.2 m walkways and crossings and never shortcut through the cold aisles.

9. Housekeeping and segregation in Zone E are strict. Refrigeration units, alarm sounders, temperature displays and emergency releases must never be blocked, switched off or adjusted except by the maintenance technician. Only the maintenance technician may release refrigeration or alarm equipment back into service after a fault, and racking in Zone E is included in the monthly documented safety inspection.

title: Site Layout and Dock Discipline
text:
1. The site is a single-storey hall of 6,000 m2 with 10 m clear height, plus a small office annex, set in a fenced yard of about 3,500 m2. Everyone learns the layout on day one: six marked zones A to F inside the hall, 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height on the yard side, and a marked driver waiting area outside. Drivers never enter the hall.

2. Zone A is receiving, 800 m2 in front of inbound Doors 1-4. Unloading, counting and inspection happen here. Nothing moves past Zone A until paperwork is checked, goods are inspected and booked into the system. Pedestrians keep to the 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways and crossings, clear of reversing trailers and forklifts.

3. Zone B is bulk storage, 2,200 m2 of high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions. It is served by the 4.0 m wide main transport aisles and the 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles, where only one truck works at a time. Zone C is picking, 1,200 m2 of ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from Zone B. Zone D is dispatch, 900 m2 of outbound staging in front of outbound Doors 5-8 for wrapped and labelled pallets only.

4. Zone E is the cold zone, a 300 m2 enclosed store held between +2 °C and +8 °C with alarms and a manual verification each shift. Its doors, curtains and seals stay closed except for immediate movements. Zone F is services and control, 600 m2 for value-added packing, quarantine, returns inspection and the separate 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. Hazmat sits only in that cage, never more than 4,000 kg at a time.

5. Dock discipline is absolute: Doors 1-4 are inbound only, Doors 5-8 are outbound only. The dispatcher assigns every carrier a door and a time slot. No trailer approaches, docks or is opened without dispatcher release, and no forklift enters a trailer until it is correctly docked, braked, chocked and its leveller is confirmed in place.

6. The yard is a controlled traffic area. The limit is 15 km/h for our electric fleet and for all visiting trailers and vans, falling to 5 km/h walking pace wherever people and trucks meet — pedestrian zones, crossings and the dock ramps. Inside the building the limit is 10 km/h throughout. Pedestrians cross yard routes only at marked crossings and never walk behind a reversing vehicle.

7. Waiting and separation rules protect everyone. After docking, drivers wait in the marked waiting area until called, in vest and S3 footwear if exceptionally authorised into a controlled area. Warehouse staff do not invite drivers onto the floor. Pallets, wrap, cages and jacks are never staged on walkways, in front of dock doors, fire exits or the hazmat cage, or against yellow barriers.

8. The shift supervisor in charge of the 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 shift, including any Saturday morning overtime, enforces layout and dock discipline on the floor. Entering a dock, ramp or leveller zone without confirmation, using the wrong doors, blocking aisles or walkways, or wedging open Zone E doors is treated as a safety incident and reported under the incident procedure.

title: Racking and Stacking Limits
text:
1. Bulk pallet storage is only in Zone B, the 2,200 m2 high-bay area with 2,400 pallet positions in fixed pallet racking. No bulk pallets are stored in Zone A receiving, Zone C pick faces except for replenishment, Zone D staging except for wrapped outbound pallets, or outside the racking and marked block-stack areas. Racking in the 300 m2 Zone E cold store and the racking used for quarantine in Zone F follow the same rules.

2. Each rack bay carries at most 2,700 kg total, including the weight of the pallets themselves. This limit is marked on the bay and applies at all times, on both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and on any Saturday morning overtime. No additional pallet may be placed into a bay that is already at its marked load or that would exceed 2,700 kg with the next pallet added.

3. The bay limit is built on the site pallet rule: a pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. In practice this means a 2,700 kg bay holds at most two full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, never three. Operators must use the WMS weight or the labelled pallet weight before put-away and must not guess. Any overweight, unstable or damaged pallet is refused for high-bay put-away and reported to the shift supervisor.

4. Free block-stacking outside the racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total height, including the pallet. Both limits apply together — whichever is reached first governs. Block stacks are permitted only in marked floor areas, never in the 4.0 m main transport aisles, the 3.0 m rack storage aisles, on pedestrian walkways, in front of dock doors 1-8, fire exits or the hazmat cage, or against yellow barriers.

5. Stacking must be stable and square. Pallets are placed level, fully supported, with no overhang beyond the rack beams or the stack base, no leaning against uprights, and no mixed unstable loads at height. Stretch wrap and labels must be intact before lifting to height. The 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t and the 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t are used only within their rated capacity, with forks at 100-150 mm for travel and loads raised or lowered only when the truck is stationary.

6. Racking must never be climbed, used as a ladder, loaded by hand from height, or struck to force a pallet into position. Only the reach trucks and counterbalance forklifts place and retrieve high-bay pallets. Hand pallet jacks and electric pallet jacks are never used for high-bay work. Nothing may be hung from, bolted to or leaned against racking, and refrigeration units, sensors and sprinklers under the 10 m clear height must be kept clear.

7. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician carries out the inspection across Zone B and the racking in Zones E and F, checking uprights, beams, bracing, fixings, beam locks, load notices and floor fixings for impact, deformation, corrosion or missing parts. The result is recorded, signed and kept for audit, and every repair is logged.

8. Any damage found or caused must be reported the same shift. The operator who sees or causes an impact stops work in that bay, makes the area safe without entering under a suspect load, and informs the shift supervisor immediately. The shift supervisor isolates the bay, prohibits further put-away into it, and calls the maintenance technician the same shift. If stock is at risk of falling, the area is barriered off until cleared.

9. Only the maintenance technician may release racking back into service after damage or repair. A damaged bay stays empty and marked out of service until inspected, repaired and signed off. Temporary propping, straightening by forklift, or reloading a damaged bay to keep put-away moving is prohibited. Damaged pallets or goods found during the check go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found.

10. Both shift supervisors enforce these limits identically on every shift. Exceeding a bay load, exceeding 3 pallets high or 4.0 m in block storage, storing outside marked areas, or reloading unreleased damaged racking is treated as a safety incident and reported under the incident procedure. New starters learn Zone B limits and reporting on day one before working unsupervised.

title: Hazmat Storage Limits
text:
1. Hazardous goods may be stored only in the separate ventilated hazmat cage in Zone F, as required by PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The cage is a fixed 60 m2 enclosure inside the 600 m2 Zone F services and control area, fitted with mechanical ventilation, locked access and hazmat signage. No other zone, rack, floor area or trailer is an approved hazmat store.

2. The maximum stock in the cage at any one time is 4,000 kg total, including the weight of the pallets, packaging and containment. The limit applies continuously, on both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts, on any Saturday morning overtime, and overnight and at weekends when the hall is unoccupied. It is never averaged over a day or a week.

3. The cage limit is built on the site pallet rule that a pallet, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. In practice this means the cage holds at most 4 full-weight 1,000 kg pallets, and fewer if pallets are bulky, require segregation gaps, or are held in spill trays or overpacks. Operators must use the booked WMS weight or the labelled pallet weight before put-away and must not guess.

4. Hazmat never sits anywhere else on site, even briefly. It must not be staged in Zone A receiving, put to bulk racking in Zone B, held on pick faces in Zone C, staged in Zone D dispatch, stored in the Zone E cold store, or left in general quarantine, returns inspection, packing, dock, aisle or yard areas.
