Pallets awaiting put-away to the cage remain on the inbound trailer or on a marked holding position under supervision until cage space is confirmed.

5. The cage itself must be kept fit for use. Ventilation must run at all times and must never be switched off, blocked by pallets, wrap or equipment, or adjusted except by the maintenance technician. The cage door stays locked except for immediate put-away, picking or inspection, access is limited to instructed staff, and smoking, naked flames, charging of trucks or scanners, and storage of combustibles are prohibited inside and within the marked clear zone outside.

6. Every hazmat pallet in the cage must be labelled, sealed, upright and stable, with its safety data sheet reference recorded in the system. Incompatible goods are segregated inside the cage according to their labels and data sheets and never stacked on top of each other. Block-stacking inside the cage follows the site rule of 3 pallets high and 4.0 m maximum, and racking, bunds, trays and floor markings must be kept clear and intact.

7. Put-away to and removal from the cage is by authorised forklift operators only, using the electric fleet within rated capacity, at 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings, ramps and where people and trucks meet. Pallets are placed squarely, fully supported and never forced against the mesh, ventilation ducts or doors. The operator confirms the running cage total in the WMS before each put-away and stops if the next pallet would exceed 4,000 kg.

8. The running total is monitored every shift. The shift supervisor in charge checks the booked cage stock against the 4,000 kg limit during the shift, and stock controllers include the cage in the daily cycle-count rotation without exceeding access rules. Any labelling error, leaking package, damaged pallet or ventilation or alarm fault found in or around the cage is reported to the shift supervisor the same shift for action under PR-13 and PR-09.

9. If a delivery or return would take the cage over 4,000 kg, it must not be unloaded into the cage or decanted elsewhere. The inbound operator or returns staff holds the goods, informs the shift supervisor and the dispatcher immediately, and the shift supervisor informs the warehouse manager the same shift. Only the warehouse manager may authorise expedited outbound removal or a controlled refusal, and no hazmat is ever stored outside the cage to solve a space problem.

10. Both shift supervisors enforce these limits identically on every shift. Storing hazmat outside the 60 m2 cage, exceeding 4,000 kg, blocking ventilation, leaving the cage unlocked or placing incompatible goods together is treated as a safety incident and reported under the incident procedure. New starters learn the cage location, limit and reporting rule on day one before working unsupervised.

title: Spills, Quarantine and Damaged Goods
text:
1. Any spillage on site is treated as a hazard until made safe, under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response and PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. This covers leaks from pallets, damaged packaging, oil or hydraulic fluid from trucks, and water, ice or condensation in and around Zone E. Anyone who finds or causes a spill stops work around it, warns others, and informs the shift supervisor immediately.

2. The immediate response is to contain without taking risks. The operator stops the truck clear of the spill, lowers forks, applies the parking brake, and keeps pedestrians clear using the 3 m clearance rule. Ignition sources are removed near flammable spills, cage ventilation is left running, and Zone E doors are kept closed. No one walks through, hoses down, or drives through a spill to keep goods flowing.

3. Personal protection is mandatory during clean-up. High-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear remain required with no exceptions, plus gloves, eye protection and, for hazmat, the equipment stated on the label and safety data sheet. Contaminated PPE and absorbents are disposed of as instructed and never put in the cardboard baler or general waste. Anyone feeling unwell leaves the area and reports to the shift supervisor.

4. Hazmat spills in or around the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F follow PR-13 strictly. Access is limited to instructed staff, the cage door is controlled, ventilation and spill trays are kept clear, and incompatible absorbents are never mixed. The shift supervisor informs the warehouse manager the same shift, the maintenance technician is called to check ventilation and equipment, and the incident is reported under the incident procedure.

5. Damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found. This applies to impact damage, crushed or leaking pallets, failed wrap or labels, cold-chain excursions, and any pallet refused for high-bay put-away or found during the monthly racking inspection. Goods are moved by authorised forklift operators at 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at crossings and ramps, or by hand jack for small stable moves, and are never left in Zones A to E, in aisles, on walkways, or in front of dock doors.

6. Quarantine is a marked, segregated area inside the 600 m2 Zone F, separate from returns inspection, value-added packing and the hazmat cage. Quarantined stock is labelled HOLD, booked to quarantine in the WMS, and physically separated so it cannot be picked, replenished to Zone C, or staged in Zone D. Only stock controllers, returns staff, the shift supervisor and the warehouse manager may move goods into or out of quarantine status.

7. Every quarantine placement is recorded the same shift. The record shows date, zone and bay of origin, pallet weight up to the 1,000 kg maximum, description of damage, WMS reference, and name of the finder and the shift supervisor informed. Stock controllers include quarantine in the daily cycle-count rotation to keep system and floor aligned. No adjustment is posted without a second count.

8. Damaged-goods decisions follow fixed approvals. The shift supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR and the final disposition of inspected returns into restock, rework or scrap. The warehouse manager signs off any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR and the annual stocktake results. Returns staff propose restock, rework or scrap after inspecting every unit within the 14-day returns rule, but only the approver releases the decision.

9. Disposition is controlled. Restock is only to its correct Zone B, E or cage location after re-inspection, re-wrap and re-label; rework is only in Zone F packing; scrap is segregated, labelled and removed without blocking walkways, fire exits or the hazmat clear zone. Hazmat scrap never goes outside the cage except in sealed, labelled containment for authorised removal.

10. Both shift supervisors enforce these rules identically on the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and on any Saturday morning overtime. Failing to report a spill, cleaning a hazmat spill without correct PPE, leaving damaged goods outside quarantine, or releasing quarantined stock without the correct approval is treated as a safety incident. New starters learn spill reporting and the quarantine location on day one before working unsupervised.

title: Incident Reporting
text:
1. Every safety event on site is reportable, whether or not anyone is hurt. This includes any injury or ill health, any near miss, any contact between a truck, trailer or load and racking, barriers, doors, levellers or building fabric, any breach of speed limits, pedestrian, dock, PPE or seat-belt rules, any spill or leak, any Zone E temperature excursion, any hazmat, cage, quarantine or stacking-limit breach, and any fire, smoke, alarm or evacuation. If in doubt, report it as an incident.

2. Reporting starts with an immediate verbal report to the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. The person involved or the first person to find the event stops work in the area, makes it safe if possible without taking risks, warns others, and informs the shift supervisor at once. Powered trucks involved stay parked with forks lowered and brake applied until released. The area is not tidied or reloaded before the supervisor has seen it.

3. The shift supervisor owns incident response on that shift. This covers both the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shifts and any Saturday morning overtime. The supervisor attends the scene, ensures first aid and protection of people first, isolates trucks, bays, docks or walkways as needed, calls the maintenance technician for equipment, racking or refrigeration checks, and informs the dispatcher if dock slots at Doors 1-8 or outbound loads are affected.

4. Every incident is then put in writing the same shift it happens. The operator or staff member involved completes the standard incident report with date, time, zone and exact location, people and trucks involved, description of what happened, and names of witnesses. Where relevant it records pallet weights up to the 1,000 kg maximum, bay loads against the 2,700 kg limit, cage totals against the 4,000 kg limit, and WMS references. The report is handed to the shift supervisor before the end of the shift.

5. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report, as required by the site responsibility rules. The review checks facts, confirms immediate actions taken, identifies whether goods must go to quarantine in Zone F the same day, whether a truck, bay, dock leveller or Zone E area must stay out of service, and whether a second count is needed before any stock adjustment. Incomplete or unclear reports are returned for correction the same shift.

6. Serious events are escalated the same shift. The shift supervisor informs the warehouse manager immediately of any injury requiring more than first aid, any rack collapse or at-risk load, any hazmat spill or ventilation failure, any fire or evacuation, any trailer or dock failure, and any event stopping inbound at Doors 1-4 or outbound at Doors 5-8. Nothing is restarted after such an event without the supervisor's explicit release, and racking or trucks only on the maintenance technician's release with the repair logged.

7. Follow-up is tracked, not filed away. The shift supervisor records corrective actions, names the owner and due date, and checks completion on the next shifts through handover under PR-15 End-of-shift handover. Repeated breaches, such as speeding, leaving walkways, blocking yellow barriers or driving without authorisation, lead to suspension of authorisation under hs.ch01.s1 and referral to the warehouse manager. Damage values feed the write-off approvals: supervisor up to 500 EUR, warehouse manager above 500 EUR.

8. Reports and actions are traceable and available for audit. Completed incident reports, supervisor reviews and evidence of corrective actions are kept together and made available to the warehouse manager and both shift supervisors. Stock controllers, inbound, picking, returns, dispatch and maintenance staff must cooperate with recounts, inspections and monthly racking checks arising from incidents. No incident record is altered after review; new information is added as a signed supplement.

9. New starters learn this system on day one before working unsupervised. They learn the Zones A to F layout, the 1.2 m walkways and crossings, the 10 km/h, 15 km/h and 5 km/h limits, the PPE and seat-belt rules, and the single rule for anything going wrong: stop, make safe, tell the shift supervisor immediately, and write it down the same shift.

title: Evacuation and Assembly
text:
1. Evacuation applies to the whole site on the same rule: when the fire alarm sounds, when smoke or fire is found, on instruction from the shift supervisor in charge or the warehouse manager, or under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Everyone in the 6,000 m2 hall, the office annex and the 3,500 m2 yard leaves the building immediately. No one stays to finish a pick, wrap a pallet, close paperwork or fetch personal items.

2. Stop work safely before leaving if seconds allow and it is safe to do so. Forklift operators lower forks to the floor, apply the parking brake, switch off the truck where fitted and leave the key in place, clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and dock doors. Inbound, picking, packing, dispatch and returns staff leave pallets where they are, leave dock levellers and Zone E doors as they are, and do not drive any truck to the exit.

3. Leave by the nearest safe signed fire exit on foot. Walk, do not run, keep high-visibility vest and S3 footwear on, and follow the 1.2 m yellow-barrier walkways and marked crossings as far as the exit route allows. Never use dock doors 1-8, levellers or trailer beds as escape routes, never walk behind reversing trailers, and never re-enter rack aisles in Zone B, the hazmat cage in Zone F or the Zone E cold store to retrieve goods or scanners.

4. Drivers in the marked waiting area and any authorised visitors or contractors leave with everyone else. Warehouse staff do not invite drivers into the hall to search for their carrier, and dispatchers do not release any trailer at Doors 1-8 during evacuation. Pedestrians cross yard routes only at marked crossings, keep clear of manoeuvring vehicles, and move directly to the assembly point.

5. The assembly point is at the marked area by the north fence, outside the fenced yard and clear of dock traffic and emergency access. All staff, visitors, contractors and drivers report there immediately and stay together by shift and work area. No one waits in the office annex, in cars, at the dock ramps or along the fence line, and no one leaves the assembly point until released.

6. Roll call is taken at the assembly point before anyone re-enters the building. The shift supervisor in charge of the 06:00-14:00 or 14:00-22:00 shift, or any Saturday morning overtime, runs the roll call with the lists of staff on shift, authorised operators, visitors and booked carriers from the dispatcher. Names are checked off one by one, missing persons are identified at once, and no group, truck or load is reported complete until every person is accounted for.

7. The shift supervisor controls the scene until handover. The supervisor ensures first aid is given, keeps people clear of the building and yard routes, informs the warehouse manager immediately, calls emergency services where needed, and informs the dispatcher to hold slots at Doors 1-4 and 5-8. No information about missing persons or damage is guessed; new information is reported to the supervisor at the assembly point.

8. No one re-enters the building until the shift supervisor or warehouse manager gives explicit permission after roll call is complete and the building is declared safe. Even then, re-entry is controlled, by instruction only, to check Zone E temperature, the 60 m2 hazmat cage ventilation, racking, dock levellers and quarantined stock before normal work restarts. Trucks, bays or docks found damaged stay out of service until released by the maintenance technician with the repair logged.

9. Every evacuation, real or drill, is recorded as an incident. The shift supervisor notes date, time, zone of origin where known, roll-call result and any failure of alarms, exits, walkways, barriers or lighting, and reviews the report the same shift. An evacuation drill is run every quarter with full roll call at the north fence, and repeated absence, late arrival at the assembly point or re-entry without permission is treated as a safety breach.

title: Checks, Drills and Handover
text:
1. Routine safety checks run to a fixed rhythm on every shift and are owned by the shift supervisor in charge. They comprise the documented pre-use check of every powered truck before its first use each day under PR-10, the manual temperature verification in Zone E once per shift under PR-12, the daily cycle count on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08, and visual checks of walkways, yellow barriers, dock doors, levellers and fire exits during the shift. Results are recorded the same shift and handed to the supervisor.

2. Truck checks are completed by the operator assigned to first use that truck that day, covering brakes, steering, horn, lights and beacon, seat belts on the 6 counterbalance forklifts and 4 reach trucks, forks and chains, hydraulics, tyres, battery, emergency stop and deadman on the 8 electric pallet jacks, and the capacity plate. A truck with a safety-critical defect is tagged out of service, parked clear of the 4.0 m main aisles and doors 1-8, and reported to the supervisor for the maintenance technician to log and repair. Only the technician releases it back into service.

3. Zone E is verified each shift with the calibrated thermometer, between +2 °C and +8 °C, with time, reading and name entered in the cold-zone log and reviewed by the supervisor. Any excursion, alarm, damaged seal, curtain or door closer is reported immediately, doors are kept closed, and no new chilled put-away is made until the supervisor confirms the condition. The supervisor informs the warehouse manager and calls the maintenance technician the same shift.

4. Stock accuracy checks support safety by preventing overloads. Stock controllers run cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule covering Zones B, E, F including the 60 m2 hazmat cage and quarantine, plus the 2,400 pallet positions in Zone B. No adjustment is posted without a second count. Once a year the site shuts down for a full wall-to-wall stocktake that the warehouse manager personally signs off. Damaged goods found during counts go to quarantine in Zone F the same day.

5. Racking receives a documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician inspects uprights, beams, bracing, fixings, beam locks, load notices and floor fixings across Zone B and the racking in Zones E and F, checking for impact, deformation or missing parts against the 2,700 kg bay limit, the 1,000 kg pallet limit and the 3 pallets high and 4.0 m block-stack rule. The record is signed and kept for audit, damaged bays are isolated and stay empty until repaired and released by the technician, and every repair is logged.

6. An evacuation drill is run every quarter under PR-14, with full evacuation of the 6,000 m2 hall, office annex and 3,500 m2 yard to the assembly point by the north fence. Roll call is taken by the shift supervisor before anyone re-enters the building, and alarms, exits, walkways, barriers and lighting failures are recorded as an incident and reviewed the same shift. The drill covers the 06:00-14:00 and 14:00-22:00 shift patterns and any Saturday morning overtime roster.

7. End-of-shift handover is mandatory under PR-15 between the morning 06:00-14:00 and afternoon 14:00-22:00 shifts, and before and after any Saturday morning overtime. The outgoing shift supervisor hands over face to face to the incoming supervisor, with the log covering incidents and near misses, out-of-service trucks, bays, levellers and blocked aisles, Zone E temperature and alarms, the running 4,000 kg cage total, quarantine placements, dock slots at doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound, and outstanding maintenance and recounts.

8. Nothing is left to memory. Daily check sheets, cold-zone logs, cycle-count sheets, racking inspections, drill records, incident reports and handover entries are completed, signed and retained for audit, with new information added as a signed supplement and never overwritten. The dispatcher holds dock scheduling information, the maintenance technician holds repair logs, and both shift supervisors enforce the same standard on every shift. New starters learn the check, drill and handover rhythm on day one before working unsupervised.

title: Warehouse Manager
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Warehouse Manager is the owner-manager of Harborwick 3PL Ltd. and is accountable for the whole Port Sellow site: all operations, safety, stock integrity and service to around twenty regular clients for packed consumer goods.

2. Team led. The Warehouse Manager directly leads 2 Shift Supervisors, 2 Dispatchers, 2 Stock Controllers and 1 Maintenance Technician, and through the supervisors leads 8 Forklift Operators, 6 Inbound Operators, 10 Pickers, 4 Returns and Packing Staff and 2 Floaters, about 38-40 people in total across morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season.

3. Accountability for operations. The Warehouse Manager owns the end-to-end goods flow defined in PR-01 to PR-09 and PR-15: document-checked receiving at inbound Doors 1-4 in Zone A, put-away to Zone B, E or F only after inspection and system booking, replenishment of Zone C pick faces before each picking shift, scan-verified picking, packing and labelling, wrapping and staging in Zone D, and dispatcher-released loading at outbound Doors 5-8.

4. Accountability for safety and compliance. The Warehouse Manager is finally accountable for safe operation of the 6,000 m2 hall, 3,500 m2 yard and 8 dock doors, including enforcement of speed limits of 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, physically separated 1.2 m walkways, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear on the floor, seat belts on moving trucks, and application of PR-10 to PR-14.

5. Capacity and storage limits owned. The Warehouse Manager ensures all planning respects fixed limits: pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, rack bay maximum 2,700 kg, block stacking maximum 3 high and 4.0 m, trailer 24,000 kg on 33 positions, van 1,200 kg on 6 positions, maximum 288 full-weight pallets per shift through 4 outbound doors, cold Zone E at +2 °C to +8 °C, and hazmat cage in Zone F limited to 60 m2 ventilated space and 4,000 kg at a time.

6. Inventory integrity. The Warehouse Manager owns the principle that system stock is rack stock. Daily rotating cycle counts under PR-08, second count before any adjustment, same-day quarantine of damaged goods under PR-09, and the annual wall-to-wall stocktake are all under the Manager's final control, and only the Manager signs off the stocktake results.

7. Financial and disposition sign-offs. The Warehouse Manager personally approves any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR. Write-offs up to 500 EUR, final disposition of inspected returns after the 14-day returns inspection, and review of every incident report are delegated to the Shift Supervisor. Returns restock, rework or scrap decisions are proposed by Returns Staff in Zone F.

8. People authorisations. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises a new forklift operator to operate the all-electric fleet of 6 x 2.5 t counterbalance forklifts, 4 x 1.6 t reach trucks, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks, and only after licence and documented daily pre-use checks under PR-10. Only the Warehouse Manager approves overtime.

9. Systems and equipment assurance. The Warehouse Manager ensures availability and correct use of 20 WMS scanners, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, cardboard baler, dock levellers at every door, monthly documented racking inspections, quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point, and logged maintenance of trucks, racking and dock equipment.

10. Handover and shift control. The Warehouse Manager appoints one Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor on every shift for staff direction and incident response, owns the dispatcher-owned dock scheduling by door and time slot with drivers held in the marked waiting area, and requires a documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15 before the next shift takes charge.

title: Shift Supervisor
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Shift Supervisor runs one shift of Harborwick 3PL Ltd. at Port Sellow and is the single person in charge of the floor for that shift. Two Shift Supervisors cover the morning shift 06:00-14:00 and the afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Warehouse Manager.

2. Staff supervised on shift. The Shift Supervisor directs all floor staff present on the shift: Forklift Operators, Inbound Operators, Pickers, Returns and Packing Staff and Floaters covering absence. Dispatchers, Stock Controllers and the Maintenance Technician report to the Warehouse Manager but work to the Supervisor's floor coordination during the shift.

3. Ownership of the shift plan. The Shift Supervisor turns the day plan into work on the floor across Zones A-F: receiving at inbound Doors 1-4 in Zone A, put-away to Zone B, E or F, replenishment of Zone C pick faces before each picking shift, scan-verified picking in Zone C, packing and labelling, wrapping and staging in Zone D for outbound Doors 5-8, and returns work in Zone F. Dock door and time-slot assignment remains owned by the Dispatcher.

4. Goods-flow discipline enforced. The Shift Supervisor enforces the fixed flow under PR-01 to PR-09: no unloading before document check, no put-away before inspection and system booking, no picking without scanner tasks, every picked item scan-verified before packing, only wrapped and labelled pallets staged in Zone D, no loading without dispatcher release, and returns decided only after inspection within 14 days of delivery.

5. Safety on the floor. The Shift Supervisor enforces PR-10 to PR-14 on the shift: speed limits of 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, use of physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m storage aisles, high-visibility vests and class S3 footwear for everyone on the floor, and seat belts on moving forklifts. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area, never in the hall.

6. Limits and special zones watched. The Shift Supervisor ensures the shift respects pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, rack bay maximum 2,700 kg, block stacking maximum 3 high and 4.0 m, cold Zone E held at +2 °C to +8 °C with alarms and manual verification each shift, and hazmat only in the 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F and never more than 4,000 kg at a time. Only licensed operators authorised by the Warehouse Manager drive the 6 x 2.5 t forklifts, 4 x 1.6 t reach trucks and pallet jacks, with documented check before first use each day.

7. Incident response. The Shift Supervisor leads immediate response to any accident, injury, spill, cold-chain alarm, fire alarm or other incident on the shift, secures people and area, calls for help, preserves the scene, and ensures damaged goods go to quarantine the same day they are found. Roll call at the assembly point by the north fence is completed before anyone re-enters after evacuation.

8. Approvals delegated to the role. The Shift Supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR, decides final disposition of inspected returns as restock, rework or scrap on proposal from Returns Staff, and reviews every incident report from the shift. Write-offs above 500 EUR, stocktake results and overtime require the Warehouse Manager's approval.

9. Inventory and equipment control on shift. The Shift Supervisor supports the daily rotating cycle counts under PR-08, ensures no adjustment is posted without a second count, ensures correct use of the 20 WMS scanners, 2 stretch wrappers, baler and dock levellers, and reports faults to the Maintenance Technician for logging. Monthly racking inspections and quarterly evacuation drills are carried out as scheduled.

10. Handover between shifts. The Shift Supervisor delivers a documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15 to the next Supervisor: progress against orders, trailer and door status for Doors 1-8, Zone C replenishment state, Zone D staging, Zone E temperature status, cage quantity, incidents, quarantines, absences and open tasks. The next shift does not take charge until handover is complete.

title: Dispatcher
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Dispatcher is part of site leadership at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow and owns all transport booking and dock scheduling. Two Dispatchers cover the operation across morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Warehouse Manager and coordinating the floor with the Shift Supervisor in charge.

2. Scope of responsibility. The Dispatcher books inbound and outbound transport, assigns every carrier a dock door and a time slot, and releases outbound loads for loading under PR-01 Inbound receiving and PR-06 Outbound dispatch. No truck is unloaded before documents are checked, and no truck is loaded without dispatcher release.

3. Dock allocation owned. The Dispatcher assigns all arrivals to the eight dock doors at 1.2 m dock height: Doors 1-4 inbound only in Zone A receiving, Doors 5-8 outbound only in Zone D dispatch. Each door has its own leveller. Drivers are directed to the marked waiting area and never enter the hall, and waiting discipline is enforced with the Shift Supervisor.

4. Inbound scheduling. The Dispatcher slots inbound trailers and vans to Doors 1-4 to match Zone A capacity of 800 m2 and the availability of Inbound Operators and Forklift Operators. Arrival documents, carrier, door and time are confirmed in advance, and changes are re-slotted before arrival so no unloading starts without document check, counting and inspection.

5. Outbound scheduling and door throughput. The Dispatcher slots outbound loads to Doors 5-8 against the fixed door capacity of 3 trailer loads per door per shift. Four outbound doors therefore cap outbound promise at 12 trailer loads per shift, and all planning with clients and carriers respects that ceiling.

6. Trailer and van loads within capacity. The Dispatcher builds every load within pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, contracted curtain-side trailer 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions, and delivery van 1,200 kg on 6 positions. In practice this means a trailer takes 24 full-weight pallets and a van takes one full-weight pallet, with anything heavier routed by trailer. The maximum promise of 288 full-weight pallets per shift is never exceeded.

7. Release of outbound loads. The Dispatcher releases a load only when its pallets are fully picked, scan-verified, packed and labelled under PR-04 and PR-05, moved to Zone D, and wrapped on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D, and the released truck is loaded and sealed for its assigned door.

8. Coordination of zones and replenishment. The Dispatcher sequences inbound put-away to Zone B bulk storage, Zone E cold zone and Zone F services against outbound staging needs in Zone D, working to the Shift Supervisor's floor plan. Before each picking shift, Zone C pick faces are replenished from bulk, and outbound staging is protected so inbound does not block Doors 5-8.

9. Special loads, cold chain and hazmat. The Dispatcher schedules cold-chain loads to Zone E held at +2 °C to +8 °C with alarms and once-per-shift manual verification under PR-12, and hazmat only to the separate 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F with never more than 4,000 kg at a time under PR-13. Returns arriving within 14 days of delivery are slotted back through Zone F for inspection.

10. Records, systems and handover. The Dispatcher maintains the transport book, door-and-slot plan, carrier communications and load-release records in the WMS using the shared 20 handheld scanners, reports faults to the Maintenance Technician, and covers transport status, door status for Doors 1-8, delayed carriers and open loads in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Overtime and write-offs above 500 EUR are escalated to the Warehouse Manager.

title: Inbound Operators
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Inbound Operators unload, count and inspect all inbound goods in Zone A receiving at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. Six Inbound Operators cover morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor and through to the Warehouse Manager.

2. Place of work. The Inbound Operators work only in Zone A receiving of 800 m2 in front of inbound Doors 1-4 at 1.2 m dock height, each with its own leveller. No goods move past Zone A to Zone B bulk storage, Zone E cold zone or Zone F services until paperwork is checked, goods are inspected, and booking is complete.

3. Scheduled arrivals. The Inbound Operators work to the Dispatcher-owned door-and-slot plan under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Every carrier has an assigned door and time slot, and drivers wait in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall. No unloading starts before the assigned door is free and the Supervisor confirms labour and equipment.

4. Document check first. The Inbound Operators check delivery documents before anything is unloaded: carrier, purchase order, client, article numbers, quantities, batch and expiry dates where required, and visible transport damage. Discrepancies are stopped and escalated to the Shift Supervisor before unloading continues.

5. Unloading, counting and inspection. The Inbound Operators unload trailers and vans together with Forklift Operators, count every pallet, carton and unit against the documents, and inspect condition, labelling, packaging integrity and temperature indicators for chilled goods. Only licensed operators authorised by the Warehouse Manager drive the 6 x 2.5 t counterbalance forklifts and pallet jacks; Inbound Operators use the 12 hand pallet jacks and work within the 10 km/h indoor and 5 km/h dock-ramp limits.

6. System booking before put-away. The Inbound Operators book only inspected goods into the WMS using the shared 20 handheld scanners, applying pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg to every receipt. Only booked goods are released for put-away to Zone B, E or F under PR-02 Put-away to storage. Uninspected or unbooked goods never go to racking, pick faces or dispatch.

7. Special goods and limits. The Inbound Operators route chilled goods immediately toward Zone E held at +2 °C to +8 °C under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and hazmat only to the separate 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F, never more than 4,000 kg at a time, under PR-13 Hazmat handling. Block-stacking and rack-bay limits of 2,700 kg per bay, 3 high and 4.0 m are observed at receipt, and damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

8. Safety and pedestrian discipline. The Inbound Operators wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor without exception, use only physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, respect 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m storage aisles, and keep pedestrians clear of dock levellers and manoeuvring trucks under PR-10 Forklift operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety.

9. Counts, equipment and housekeeping. The Inbound Operators support daily rotating cycle counts under PR-08, never post an adjustment without a second count, keep Zone A clear and swept for the next arrival, and report scanner, leveller or MHE faults to the Maintenance Technician for logging. Monthly racking inspections and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point are attended as scheduled.

10. Handover and traceability. The Inbound Operators record every receipt, shortage, overage, damage and quarantine transfer in the WMS and pass receipts booked, pallets awaiting put-away, held loads, door status for Doors 1-4 and open problems to the next shift in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Returns arriving within 14 days of delivery are passed directly to Zone F without inbound booking as stock.

title: Forklift Operators
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Forklift Operators drive all mechanical handling equipment at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow and move goods between zones. Eight Forklift Operators cover morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor and through to the Warehouse Manager.

2. Authorisation to operate. No licence, no truck. Only the Warehouse Manager authorises a new forklift operator after licence verification, and only authorised operators drive under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Authorisation covers the all-electric fleet: 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t for general work, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t for the high bays, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks for small moves.

3. Place of work. The Forklift Operators work across Zones A-F in the 6,000 m2 hall and 3,500 m2 yard: Zone A receiving of 800 m2 at inbound Doors 1-4, Zone B bulk storage of 2,200 m2 with 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C picking of 1,200 m2, Zone D dispatch of 900 m2 at outbound Doors 5-8, Zone E cold zone of 300 m2, and Zone F services and control of 600 m2. Drivers wait in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall.

4. Documented daily check. Every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10: brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains, tyres, battery charge and leaks, seat belt function, and dock leveller condition at the assigned door. Defects are tagged out, reported to the Maintenance Technician for logging, and the truck is not used until released.

5. Speed and pedestrian discipline. The Forklift Operators observe 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard, and 5 km/h wherever people and trucks meet — marked pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers are never driven on, 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles are kept clear, and pedestrians have priority under PR-11 Pedestrian safety.

6. Safe driving rules. The Forklift Operators wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor without exception and wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Loads are carried low, ramps are driven straight, no passengers are carried, and trucks are parked braked with forks lowered clear of walkways and dock edges.

7. Load and storage limits. Every move respects pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, rack bay maximum 2,700 kg, and free block-stacking elsewhere limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m. Reach trucks are used in the high bays of Zone B, counterbalance trucks for loading, unloading and general work. Overweight, unstable or damaged pallets are stopped and escalated to the Shift Supervisor.

8. Goods-flow tasks. The Forklift Operators work to scanner tasks and the Supervisor's floor plan under PR-01 to PR-06: unloading with Inbound Operators in Zone A only after document check, put-away to Zone B, E or F only for inspected and WMS-booked goods using the shared 20 handheld scanners, replenishment of Zone C pick faces from bulk before each picking shift, moves of packed and labelled pallets to Zone D for wrapping on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, and loading only on dispatcher release at Doors 5-8.

9. Special goods and damage. Chilled pallets go immediately toward Zone E held at +2 °C to +8 °C under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and hazmat goes only to the separate 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F, never more than 4,000 kg at a time, under PR-13 Hazmat handling. Damaged goods found in transit go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09, and cold-chain alarms, spills or incidents are reported at once for Supervisor-led response.

10. Counts, housekeeping and handover. The Forklift Operators support daily rotating cycle counts under PR-08, never post an adjustment without a second count, keep aisles, dock approaches and levellers clear, attend monthly racking inspections and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point, and pass moves completed, pallets staged, battery states, defects and open tasks in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15.

title: Pickers
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. Ten Pickers cover morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor and through to the Warehouse Manager.

2. Place of work. The Pickers work only in Zone C picking of 1,200 m2: ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from Zone B bulk storage. Pick faces are replenished from bulk before each picking shift under PR-03 Replenishment, and Pickers never pick from empty, damaged or unreplenished locations without escalating to the Shift Supervisor.

3. Scanner-led work. The Pickers work only to WMS scanner tasks under PR-04 Order picking using the shared 20 handheld scanners. No picking without a task, no picking from a different location than instructed, and no quantity change without system confirmation and Supervisor approval.

4. Scan verification before packing. Every picked item is scan-verified before it is packed: article, batch and expiry where required, quantity and pick-face location are scanned and confirmed. Shortages, overages, damages or label mismatches are stopped, reported to the Shift Supervisor, and damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

5. Packing, labelling and transfer. The Pickers pack and label picked orders under PR-05 Packing and labelling, build stable pallets within pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, and move packed and labelled pallets to Zone D dispatch of 900 m2. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D for outbound Doors 5-8, with wrapping done on the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers.

6. Special goods discipline. Chilled picks for Zone E held at +2 °C to +8 °C are handled under PR-12 Cold-chain handling with minimum dwell time and immediate transfer, and hazmat picks only from the separate 60 m2 ventilated cage in Zone F, never more than 4,000 kg at a time, under PR-13 Hazmat handling. Cold-chain alarms or spills are reported at once for Supervisor-led response.

7. Equipment use. The Pickers use the 12 hand pallet jacks for small moves in Zone C and 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m storage aisles. No licence, no truck: the 6 x 2.5 t counterbalance forklifts, 4 x 1.6 t reach trucks and 8 electric pallet jacks are driven only by licensed operators authorised by the Warehouse Manager under PR-10, with documented check before first use each day.

8. Safety and pedestrian discipline. The Pickers wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor without exception, use only physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and respect 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps under PR-11 Pedestrian safety. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area and never enter the hall.

9. Counts, housekeeping and equipment care. The Pickers support daily rotating cycle counts under PR-08, never post an adjustment without a second count, keep pick faces, flow racks and aisles clear, clean and correctly labelled, and report scanner, racking or MHE faults to the Maintenance Technician for logging. Monthly racking inspections and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point are attended as scheduled.

10. Handover and traceability. The Pickers record every task, shortage, damage and pallet transferred to Zone D in the WMS and pass tasks completed, tasks open, replenishment needs, Zone D transfers and open problems to the next shift in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Returns arriving within 14 days of delivery are not handled as picks and are passed directly to Zone F for inspection.

title: Stock Controllers
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Stock Controllers own inventory accuracy day to day at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. Two Stock Controllers cover morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Warehouse Manager and coordinating the floor with the Shift Supervisor in charge.

2. Scope of ownership. The Stock Controllers are accountable for the principle that system stock is rack stock across Zones A-F in the 6,000 m2 hall: Zone A receiving of 800 m2, Zone B bulk storage of 2,200 m2 with 2,400 pallet positions, Zone C picking of 1,200 m2, Zone D dispatch of 900 m2, Zone E cold zone of 300 m2, and Zone F services including quarantine and the 60 m2 ventilated hazmat cage. No stock moves without WMS traceability.

3. Daily cycle counts. The Stock Controllers run cycle counts every working day on a rotating zone schedule under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, using the shared 20 handheld WMS scanners. Counts cover bulk locations, pick faces, cold locations and cage locations, and progress is directed with the Shift Supervisor so picking, replenishment and loading are not blocked.

4. Recounts before adjustments. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count. The Stock Controllers perform the recount for every discrepancy, investigate root cause with Inbound Operators, Forklift Operators and Pickers — document error, put-away error, pick error or damage — and post adjustments only after the second count confirms the variance.

5. Annual wall-to-wall stocktake. The Stock Controllers prepare and run the full wall-to-wall stocktake once a year under PR-08: freeze discipline, location sequencing, count teams, recounts of differences, and reconciliation. The stocktake results are signed off only by the Warehouse Manager, and the shutdown plan is executed with the Shift Supervisors and Dispatcher.

6. Limits and special stocks controlled. The Stock Controllers monitor pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, rack bay maximum 2,700 kg, and block stacking limited to 3 high and 4.0 m during every count, and escalate overloads at once. Hazmat stock is counted only in the Zone F cage and never more than 4,000 kg at a time under PR-13, and damaged goods found during counts go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

7. Cold-zone checks. The Stock Controllers verify Zone E chilled storage held between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. Alarms are checked, the manual temperature verification each shift is recorded, and any excursion is escalated immediately to the Shift Supervisor for response, with affected stock held and not picked or dispatched until released.

8. Damaged goods and returns integrity. The Stock Controllers track quarantine movements from Zone F, ensure returns accepted within 14 days of delivery are inspected before any restock decision, and ensure write-offs above 500 EUR go to the Warehouse Manager and write-offs up to 500 EUR go to the Shift Supervisor. No scrapped, reworked or restocked quantity re-enters book stock without WMS posting.

9. Safety and equipment discipline. The Stock Controllers wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor without exception, use only physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and work within 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps under PR-10 and PR-11. Scanner, racking and leveller faults are reported to the Maintenance Technician for logging, and monthly racking inspections and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point are attended as scheduled.

10. Records and handover. The Stock Controllers maintain count sheets, recount records, adjustment logs, temperature logs and stocktake files in the WMS and pass counts completed, variances open, recounts pending, Zone E status, cage quantity and quarantines to the next shift in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area and Doors 1-4 inbound and 5-8 outbound discipline owned by the Dispatcher is never bypassed for counting convenience.

title: Returns and Packing Staff
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Returns and Packing Staff inspect returns and carry out packing and value-added work in Zone F at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. Four staff cover morning shift 06:00-14:00 and afternoon shift 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor and through to the Warehouse Manager.

2. Place of work. The Returns and Packing Staff work only in Zone F services and control of 600 m2: value-added packing stations, quarantine area, returns inspection benches, and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. No returns, rework or quarantine stock is held outside Zone F, and hazmat never sits anywhere else.

3. Returns acceptance. The Returns and Packing Staff receive returns arriving back through Zone F within 14 days of delivery, slotted by the Dispatcher. Returns are not booked as inbound stock and are never picked as normal orders. Every return is logged in the WMS using the shared 20 handheld scanners and held for inspection before any further decision.

4. Inspection of every unit. The Returns and Packing Staff inspect every returned unit under PR-07 Returns handling: article, quantity, batch and expiry where required, packaging integrity, labelling, temperature history for chilled lines, and saleability. Damaged or suspect goods found are moved to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

5. Proposal of disposition. The Returns and Packing Staff propose restock, rework or scrap for every inspected return. Restock only for intact, in-date, correctly labelled units; rework for repackable or relabellable units; scrap for damaged, expired or unsafe units. Final disposition is decided by the Shift Supervisor, and no quantity re-enters book stock without WMS posting and Stock Controller traceability.

6. Packing, labelling and wrapping. The Returns and Packing Staff pack and label under PR-05 Packing and labelling, including value-added packing for clients, and build stable pallets within pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg. Packed and labelled pallets for dispatch are moved to Zone D of 900 m2. Only wrapped and labelled pallets are staged in Zone D, using the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, and loading at Doors 5-8 is only on dispatcher release.

7. Special goods discipline. Chilled returns for Zone E held at +2 °C to +8 °C are handled under PR-12 Cold-chain handling with minimum dwell time and manual temperature verification each shift. Hazmat returns go only to the 60 m2 ventilated cage, never more than 4,000 kg at a time, under PR-13 Hazmat handling. Alarms, spills or excursions are reported at once for Supervisor-led response.

8. Safety and equipment use. The Returns and Packing Staff wear high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the floor without exception, use only physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers, and work within 10 km/h inside, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps under PR-10 and PR-11. Small moves use the 12 hand pallet jacks; the 6 x 2.5 t forklifts, 4 x 1.6 t reach trucks and 8 electric pallet jacks are driven only by licensed operators authorised by the Warehouse Manager.

9. Counts, quarantine control and housekeeping. The Returns and Packing Staff support daily rotating cycle counts under PR-08, never post an adjustment without a second count, keep quarantine quantities identified and segregated, and respect rack bay maximum 2,700 kg and block stacking limited to 3 high and 4.0 m. Write-offs above 500 EUR go to the Warehouse Manager and up to 500 EUR to the Shift Supervisor. Scanner, wrapper, baler and racking faults are reported to the Maintenance Technician for logging.

10. Records and handover. The Returns and Packing Staff record every inspection, proposal, rework, restock, scrap and quarantine transfer in the WMS and pass returns inspected, dispositions pending, quarantine holdings, packing progress and open problems to the next shift in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Monthly racking inspections and quarterly evacuation drills with roll call at the north fence assembly point are attended as scheduled.

title: Maintenance Technician
text:
1. Position in the organisation. The Maintenance Technician maintains all trucks, racking and dock equipment at Harborwick 3PL Ltd. in Port Sellow. One Technician covers the site Monday to Friday, plus Saturday morning overtime in peak season, reporting to the Warehouse Manager and coordinating daily work with the Shift Supervisor in charge of the floor.

2. Scope of ownership. The Maintenance Technician owns the serviceable condition of the all-electric fleet, storage equipment and dock equipment across the 6,000 m2 hall, 3,500 m2 yard and 8 dock doors at 1.2 m dock height: 6 counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks, 12 hand pallet jacks, high-bay racking with 2,400 positions in Zone B of 2,200 m2, levellers at every door, 20 handheld WMS scanners, 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers and 1 cardboard baler.

3. Daily truck checks supported. The Maintenance Technician ensures every truck gets a documented check before its first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation: brakes, steering, lights, horn, forks, chains, tyres, battery charge and leaks, and seat belt function. Defective trucks are tagged out and not released until repaired. Only licensed operators authorised by the Warehouse Manager drive trucks.

4. Repair logging. The Maintenance Technician logs every repair in the maintenance log: date, equipment number, fault reported, work done, parts used, downtime and release back to operation. Faults reported by Supervisors, Operators, Pickers, Stock Controllers, Returns Staff and Dispatchers are prioritised for safety first, then for inbound Doors 1-4, Zone C replenishment and outbound Doors 5-8 continuity.

5. Racking safety inspections. The Maintenance Technician carries out the documented racking safety inspection every month under PR-10: uprights, beams, bracing, fixings, bay load notices, impact damage, beam deflection and aisle clearances. Overloads beyond rack bay maximum 2,700 kg or block stacking beyond 3 high and 4.0 m are reported at once to the Shift Supervisor. Damaged bays are unloaded, barriered off and logged until repaired.

6. Dock, wrapper and building equipment. The Maintenance Technician maintains dock levellers, dock doors, seals and dock-ramp markings, the 2 stretch wrappers, the cardboard baler and the cold Zone E alarms and doors. Pallet with load maximum 1,000 kg, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m storage aisles are protected during all maintenance work, with cones and barriers set before work starts.

7. Cold zone and hazmat support. The Maintenance Technician keeps Zone E chilled storage of 300 m2 held between +2 °C and +8 °C under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2 in Zone F under PR-13 Hazmat handling in serviceable condition. Alarm, ventilation, lighting and temperature-verification equipment faults are repaired as priority, and any excursion or spill is escalated immediately to the Shift Supervisor. Hazmat is never more than 4,000 kg at a time.

8. Safety and pedestrian discipline. The Maintenance Technician wears high-visibility vest and class S3 safety footwear on the floor without exception, wears seat belt when driving any truck for testing, and observes 10 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the yard and 5 km/h in pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps. Only physically separated 1.2 m walkways with yellow barriers are used on foot under PR-11 Pedestrian safety. Drivers remain in the marked waiting area during maintenance at the docks.

9. Evacuation and emergency support. The Maintenance Technician supports the evacuation drill every quarter under PR-14 Emergency evacuation: alarm function, emergency exits, assembly point by the north fence, and roll call before anyone re-enters. Fire equipment access, walkway barriers and dock approaches are kept clear, and damaged goods go to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09.

10. Records and handover. The Maintenance Technician maintains repair logs, monthly racking inspection records, leveller and wrapper service records and drill attendance notes, and passes defects open, trucks tagged out, bays barriered, parts awaited and work planned to the Shift Supervisors and Warehouse Manager in the documented end-of-shift handover under PR-15. Overtime and damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR are escalated to the Warehouse Manager for approval.

title: Inbound Receiving Hours and Intake
text:
1. We receive inbound goods Monday to Friday during our two operating shifts: 06:00–14:00 and 14:00–22:00. Outside these hours we receive only by prior written agreement, including peak-season Saturday morning overtime, which requires approval and available supervision.

2. All inbound intake takes place in Zone A (800 m2) through Doors 1–4, which are designated inbound only. Each dock door is 1.2 m dock height with its own leveller. No inbound vehicle will be directed to outbound Doors 5–8.

3. Every inbound delivery requires a pre-booked time slot assigned by our dispatcher. The dispatcher confirms door number, date and time window to the carrier. Carriers without a confirmed slot will be held until a slot and door become available, without liability for waiting time.

4. On arrival the driver reports to the designated check-in point and waits in the marked driver waiting area. Drivers are not permitted in the hall or in Zone A except when expressly escorted for load-securing or seal checks.

5. We apply a document-check-before-unload standard under PR-01 Inbound receiving. Before any unloading begins, our inbound operators verify the delivery note, purchase order or client advice, quantities announced, and, where applicable, seals, batch and expiry data. Nothing moves past Zone A until paperwork is checked.

6. If documents are missing, inconsistent with the booking, or show goods we have no instruction to accept, we will hold the vehicle at the door, notify the client contact, and take no further intake action until written instruction is received.

7. Once documents are accepted, we unload, count and inspect in Zone A. Counts are made against delivery documents and client advice, and visible condition, packaging integrity, labelling and pallet condition are inspected and recorded.

8. Only inspected goods are booked into the warehouse management system. Only system-booked goods are released for put-away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F. Uninspected or unbooked goods will not be put away, picked or reported as available stock.

9. Intake discrepancies — shortages, overages, misdeliveries, visible damage, or temperature or cold-chain anomalies for chilled goods — will be noted on the receiving record with photographs where practicable and reported to the client on the same working day. Damaged goods found at intake are transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

10. Receiving capacity is managed through dispatcher-controlled door scheduling to protect inspection quality and system accuracy. Where a delivery cannot be fully received within its slot due to late arrival, missing documents, or non-compliant presentation, the balance will be rescheduled to the next available inbound slot in agreement with the client.

11. All intake activity complies with site safety rules: yard speed limit 15 km/h and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, physically separated 1.2 m pedestrian walkways, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor, and handling only by trained staff using checked equipment.

title: Outbound Dispatch Capacity and Cut-Offs
text:
1. We dispatch outbound goods Monday to Friday during our two operating shifts: 06:00–14:00 and 14:00–22:00. Outside these hours, including peak-season Saturday morning overtime, we dispatch only by prior written agreement and approved overtime with available supervision.

2. All outbound loading takes place from Zone D (900 m2) through Doors 5–8, which are designated outbound only. Each dock door is 1.2 m dock height with its own leveller. No outbound vehicle will be loaded at inbound Doors 1–4.

3. Every outbound collection requires a pre-booked time slot and door assignment by our dispatcher under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. The dispatcher confirms door number, date and time window to the carrier and the client. Vehicles arriving without a confirmed slot or outside their window will be held until a door becomes available, without liability for waiting time.

4. On arrival the driver reports to the designated check-in point and waits in the marked driver waiting area. Drivers are not permitted in the hall or in Zone D except when expressly escorted for load-securing or seal checks.

5. Only wrapped, labelled pallets staged in Zone D for their assigned outbound door will be loaded. Under PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-06, every picked item is scan-verified before packing, then labelled, moved to Zone D, stretch-wrapped and staged. Unwrapped, unlabelled or unstaged goods will not be loaded.

6. No load is loaded or sealed without dispatcher release. Release requires a complete, system-confirmed order, correct staging in Zone D, and transport documents checked against the load. The truck is loaded by trained staff and sealed, with seal number recorded.

7. Our maximum committed outbound capacity per shift is 288 full-weight pallets. This is built on fixed site capacities: a pallet with load may weigh at most 1,000 kg, our contracted curtain-side trailers carry 24,000 kg on 33 floor positions and therefore take 24 full-weight pallets, and each of our 4 outbound doors handles 3 trailer loads per shift.

8. The calculation is therefore 4 doors x 3 trailer loads x 24 full-weight pallets = 288 full-weight pallets per shift. This is the most we can promise a client per shift across all clients combined, and bookings beyond this limit will be offered the next available shift.

9. For smaller consignments our delivery van carries 1,200 kg on 6 positions, equivalent to one full-weight pallet. Anything heavier than 1,200 kg goes by trailer and counts against trailer capacity above. Van collections are also scheduled through the dispatcher to an assigned outbound door and time slot.

10. To protect same-shift loading, we apply load-release cut-offs per shift: orders for the morning shift must be fully confirmed and released to picking no later than 15:00 on the previous working day, and orders for the afternoon shift no later than 07:00 on the same working day. Orders for chilled goods in Zone E and goods in the Zone F hazmat cage are subject to the same cut-offs, plus handling checks under PR-12 and PR-13.

11. Orders received after the cut-off, incomplete orders, or orders requiring replenishment from bulk Zone B beyond the pre-shift replenishment will be planned for the next available shift and confirmed to the client. Replenishment of pick faces in Zone C is completed before each picking shift and does not interrupt staged outbound loads.

12. All dispatch activity complies with site safety rules: yard speed limit 15 km/h and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones, crossings and dock ramps, physically separated 1.2 m pedestrian walkways, 4.0 m main transport aisles, mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor, and handling only by trained staff using checked equipment.

title: Order Accuracy and Pick-Pack Standard
text:
1. We pick all customer orders in Zone C (1,200 m2) from ground-level pick faces and flow racks. No picking takes place from bulk storage in Zone B, from quarantine, or directly from receiving in Zone A. Only system-booked, available stock is presented for picking.

2. Before each picking shift, the pick faces in Zone C are replenished from bulk under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Replenishment is completed before picking starts and is confirmed in the warehouse management system, so pickers start each shift with full, system-accurate faces.

3. If a pick face cannot be fully replenished due to shortage in bulk, allocation across clients, or blocked stock in quarantine, cold-check hold or hazmat control, the affected order lines are flagged as short in the system and notified to the client before dispatch staging. We do not substitute SKUs, batches or expiry profiles without written client instruction.

4. All picking is performed as scanner-directed tasks under PR-04 Order picking. Pickers work only against tasks issued on the 20 shared handheld WMS scanners. Paper picks, memory picks and re-picks without a system task are not permitted.

5. Every picked item is scan-verified at the pick face. The scanner confirms correct Zone C location, SKU, quantity and, where applicable, batch, serial and expiry required by the client advice. A pick that does not scan-match cannot be confirmed and must be re-checked or escalated to the shift supervisor on duty.

6. After scan verification, goods are packed and labelled under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Packing checks outer condition, quantity per carton, and pallet build to the 1,000 kg maximum per pallet including load. Each carton and pallet is labelled to client specification before leaving Zone C. Unlabelled or mislabelled units are not moved to dispatch.

7. Packed, labelled goods are moved to Zone D (900 m2) and stretch-wrapped on our semi-automatic wrappers, then staged by outbound door and load. Only wrapped, labelled pallets staged for their assigned door in Zone D are eligible for loading under PR-06. Staging preserves separation by client, order and delivery drop.

8. We operate a scan-verified pack-to-stage chain with no gaps: replenished face to scanner task to scan-verified pick to labelled pack to wrapped stage to dispatcher release. Any break in scanning, labelling or staging removes the pallet from the load until corrected and re-verified.

9. Picks requiring special handling follow the same accuracy standard plus their control procedure: chilled picks in Zone E (+2 °C to +8 °C) under PR-12 Cold-chain handling with exposure minimised and cold-chain anomalies reported, and hazmat picks from the ventilated 60 m2 cage in Zone F under PR-13 with the 4,000 kg cage limit observed. Value-added packing work in Zone F is completed and re-verified before transfer to Zone D.

10. Damaged or suspect goods found during replenishment, picking or packing are excluded from the order and transferred to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. They are not re-picked, re-packed or reported as available. Returns and rework decisions are handled separately in Zone F under PR-07.

11. Our order accuracy standard is measured at dispatch staging: correct SKU, correct quantity, correct batch and expiry where required, correct label, and correct staging to the correct door and load. Errors detected before dispatcher release are corrected, re-scanned and re-staged. Errors reported after delivery are logged as incidents, reviewed by the shift supervisor, and reported with root cause and corrective action.

12. All pick-pack activity is performed by trained staff on the active shift — pickers in Zone C, forklift operators for replenishment and stage moves, and dispatchers for release — under the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. Work complies with site safety rules: 10 km/h inside, 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles kept clear, physically separated 1.2 m walkways, and mandatory high-visibility vests, class S3 footwear and forklift seat belts when moving.

title: Storage Zones and Capacity Limits
text:
1. Client stock is stored only in designated storage locations: bulk storage in Zone B (2,200 m2), chilled storage in Zone E (300 m2), and controlled storage in Zone F (600 m2), with live pick quantities presented in Zone C (1,200 m2). Zones A (800 m2) and D (900 m2) are transit zones only and are not storage locations.

2. Zone B is our general bulk storage for packed consumer goods. It provides high-bay pallet racking with 2,400 pallet positions, supplemented by defined block-stacking areas outside the racking. Allocation of racking versus block locations is made by the warehouse management system under PR-02 Put-away to storage.

3. Every pallet on site, load included, may weigh at most 1,000 kg. This single limit governs all racking, stacking, handling equipment and transport calculations. Pallets exceeding 1,000 kg will not be put away, replenished or dispatched until re-built and re-weighed.

4. Each rack bay in Zone B carries at most 2,700 kg in total. In practice this limits loading to two full-weight pallets per bay, or three lighter pallets provided their combined weight does not exceed 2,700 kg. The system blocks put-away that would exceed the bay limit, and over-weight placements are prohibited even if a position is physically free.

5. Free block-stacking outside the racking is limited to 3 pallets high and 4.0 m total stack height. Stacks must be stable, uniformly built, and placed only in marked block locations that keep 4.0 m main transport aisles and 3.0 m rack storage aisles clear. Damaged pallets, leaning stacks or stacks blocking walkways, doors or emergency routes will not be accepted for storage.

6. Zone C holds only the replenished working quantity for current picking shifts. It consists of ground-level pick faces and flow racks fed from Zone B before each picking shift under PR-03. Bulk reserve remains in Zone B and is not reported or picked from Zone C locations.

7. Zone E is our chilled storage of 300 m2, held between +2 °C and +8 °C with alarms and manual temperature verification each shift under PR-12. Only goods requiring chilled storage are placed in Zone E, and only up to its physical and system-assigned capacity. Non-chilled goods will not be stored in Zone E to create space elsewhere.

8. Zone F provides value-added packing, quarantine, returns inspection and the separate ventilated hazmat cage of 60 m2. General client stock is not stored in quarantine or in the packing and inspection work areas, which are held clear for processing.

9. All hazardous goods are stored only inside the Zone F hazmat cage and never elsewhere on site. The cage holds at most 4,000 kg at any time, equivalent to 4 full-weight pallets of 1,000 kg. Bookings that would exceed this limit will be refused or scheduled for a later slot, and hazmat picks are controlled under PR-13.

10. Put-away follows the booked-stock rule: only inspected goods booked into the warehouse management system in Zone A are released to Zone B, E or F. Uninspected, unbooked or quarantined goods are not put away and are not reported as available. Damaged goods found at any stage go to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09.

11. Storage on site is within a single-storey hall of 6,000 m2 with 10 m clear height. All storage activity complies with site safety and handling rules: handling only by trained staff using checked electric equipment, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings, physically separated 1.2 m walkways, and mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear.

12. Where a client requires capacity beyond available racking, chilled or hazmat limits, we will confirm available positions, offer the next available storage slot, or agree overflow handling in writing. We do not exceed pallet, bay, height or cage limits to accommodate volume.

title: Cycle Counts and Annual Stocktake
text:
1. We count stock every working day, Monday to Friday, on both operating shifts. Cycle counting is a permanent control under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts and is performed on a rotating zone schedule that covers all storage locations in Zone B, Zone C, Zone E and Zone F, including bulk racking, block stacks, pick faces, the chilled store and the hazmat cage.

2. The rotating schedule is set by the stock controllers and confirmed by the warehouse manager. It ensures every storage zone is counted in rotation without disrupting receiving in Zone A or staging and loading in Zone D. The client is informed in advance which zones and SKUs are scheduled on any day.

3. All cycle counts are performed by stock controllers, supported by trained floor staff under the shift supervisor in charge. Counts are directed as system tasks on the handheld WMS scanners against live system quantities. Counts from memory, paper lists or unassigned re-checks are not accepted.

4. Goods in transit in Zone A and Zone D are not cycle-counted as stored stock. Only inspected goods booked into the system and put away to Zone B, E or F, plus working quantities in Zone C, are counted as inventory. Goods in quarantine remain system-blocked and are counted separately for control but never reported as available.

5. Each cycle count is a blind first count followed by system comparison. Where the first count matches the system, the location is confirmed and closed. Where it differs, the location is frozen for movements until resolved and a recount is ordered the same shift.

6. No inventory adjustment is ever posted without a second count. The recount is performed by a different person from the first counter, normally the second stock controller or the shift supervisor, using the same scanner procedure and checking pallet integrity, label, batch and expiry, and bay and location identity.

7. If the recount confirms the difference, the stock controllers investigate cause — mis-put-away, replenishment error, pick error, damage or paperwork lag — and propose an adjustment with evidence. Small damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR are approved by the shift supervisor; any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager under PR-09.

8. Cycle-count results, recounts and approved adjustments are recorded in the warehouse management system the same working day. The client is notified the same working day of any confirmed discrepancy affecting its available stock, with quantity, location, cause where known, and corrective action.

9. Once a year we shut down operations for a full wall-to-wall stocktake of the entire site. The date is agreed with clients in advance, all movements in and out are stopped, Zone C faces are closed, and every pallet and pick location in Zones B, C, E and F is counted, including quarantine and hazmat cage holdings.

10. The annual stocktake is prepared, supervised and personally signed off by the warehouse manager as accountable for the whole site. The sign-off confirms scope completed, recounts completed, adjustments posted, and closing stock by client, SKU, batch and location. No annual result is issued to clients without this sign-off.

11. All counting activity follows site safety and handling rules: work only by authorised staff on the supervised shift, handling only with checked equipment, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles kept clear, and mandatory high-visibility vests and class S3 safety footwear on the warehouse floor.

12. Cycle counts and the annual stocktake together provide our inventory accuracy commitment: counted every day, corrected only after recount, and closed once a year by full count and manager sign-off, so the stock in the system remains the stock on the rack.

title: Stock Reporting and Accountability
text:
1. Our warehouse management system is the single source of truth for stock. Only inspected goods booked in Zone A and put away to Zone B, Zone E or Zone F, plus working quantities in Zone C, are reported as available. Goods in receiving in Zone A, staging in Zone D, quarantine, or unbooked holds are never reported as available.

2. Day-to-day ownership of system accuracy sits with our 2 stock controllers under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts. They own the rotating count schedule, recounts, investigations and proposed adjustments, and they keep system locations, batches, expiries and pallet identities aligned with the physical rack.

3. We report cycle-count outcomes every working day, Monday to Friday. The same working day we confirm to the client quantities counted, locations closed without difference, and any confirmed discrepancy affecting its stock with quantity, location, cause where known and corrective action. No adjustment is posted without a second count by a different person.

4. We issue a weekly stock summary per client by 12:00 on the first working day of the following week. It shows opening balance, receipts booked, picks dispatched, returns restocked, approved adjustments and write-offs, and closing balance by SKU, batch and expiry, split by Zone B, Zone C, Zone E and Zone F cage holdings.

5. We issue a monthly closing stock statement within three working days of month-end. It reconciles the weekly summaries to the system closing balance, lists blocked quantities in quarantine separately, and confirms chilled and hazmat holdings against their limits. It is the binding record for billing and client closing.

6. Accountability is fixed. Stock controllers prepare all counts and reports. The shift supervisor in charge reviews every daily report, recount result and incident report on its shift and approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR. The warehouse manager, as accountable for the whole site, signs off the annual stocktake results and any write-off above 500 EUR.

7. No daily, weekly, monthly or annual report is issued to a client without named review. Daily reports carry the reviewing shift supervisor's name, weekly and monthly statements carry stock-controller preparation and supervisor review, and the annual wall-to-wall result carries the warehouse manager's personal sign-off before release.

8. Discrepancies that affect availability trigger immediate escalation, not just routine reporting. Shortages in bulk blocking replenishment, damage found during counting, and cold-chain or hazmat anomalies are notified the same shift to the client contact, with the location frozen until recount and disposition under PR-09, PR-12 or PR-13.

9. System corrections follow a closed loop. The recount confirms the difference, the cause is recorded, the adjustment or write-off is approved at the correct level, and the correction is posted in the system the same working day with evidence retained. Unapproved, verbal or spreadsheet-only corrections are not valid and will not be reported.

10. Client data is separated by client, order and location in every report. We do not co-mingle client stocks in reporting, substitute SKUs, batches or expiry profiles, or disclose one client's holdings to another. Returns awaiting inspection in Zone F are reported only as pending inspection until final disposition is approved by the shift supervisor.

11. All reporting work is performed on supervised shifts using the 20 handheld WMS scanners and system-generated records. Routine reporting does not require overtime. Where a client requests ad-hoc counts, audits or out-of-hours statements, we schedule them by written agreement subject to available supervision and overtime approval by the warehouse manager only.

title: Damaged Goods and Quarantine
text:
1. Quarantine is the physically segregated, system-blocked holding area inside Zone F (600 m2) for damaged, suspect and non-conforming goods. It is the only place damaged goods may be held.
