Damaged goods are never left in Zones A, B, C, D or E, never stored in the hazmat cage unless they are hazmat under PR-13, and never reported as available stock.

2. Any damaged, leaking, crushed, wet, contaminated, mislabelled or otherwise suspect goods found at receiving, put-away, replenishment, picking, packing, dispatch staging, cycle counting or cold-chain checks are segregated to quarantine the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.

3. The person finding the damage stops further handling of the affected pallet or units, preserves labels, batches and evidence, and calls the shift supervisor. The goods are moved to quarantine by trained staff using checked equipment, with a quarantine tag showing date, time, location found, SKU, quantity, reason and finder name.

4. On arrival in quarantine the goods are booked as blocked in the warehouse management system. Blocked quantities are excluded from available stock, from replenishment, from pick tasks in Zone C and from dispatcher release in Zone D. They are counted separately for control but listed only as blocked.

5. Every quarantine entry is recorded with photographs where practicable, delivery or order reference, batch and expiry where applicable, and extent and suspected cause of damage. The record is notified to the client the same working day, with quantity held, location blocked and next steps pending inspection.

6. Quarantine is inspected and dispositioned without delay. The shift supervisor reviews every quarantine case and incident report on its shift, orders a second check where quantities or cause are uncertain, and decides containment — hold for client instruction, propose restock after rework, or propose scrap. No adjustment is ever posted without a second count by a different person.

7. No damaged goods leave quarantine without approved disposition. Goods confirmed as saleable are returned to system stock only after re-inspection, re-labelling where needed and system release. Goods requiring rework pass through Zone F packing under PR-05 and are re-verified before transfer. Goods confirmed as unsaleable are proposed for write-off and scrap.

8. Write-off approval thresholds are fixed. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR and the final record of disposition. Any damaged-goods write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager as accountable for the whole site. Unapproved, verbal or spreadsheet-only write-offs are not valid and will not be reported.

9. Approved write-offs and scrapping are posted in the system the same working day, with evidence retained and reported in the daily cycle-count outcome, the weekly summary and the monthly closing statement. Scrapped goods are disposed of per client instruction and waste rules, and the cardboard baler is used only for packaging waste, never for product.

10. Chilled goods found damaged or outside +2 °C to +8 °C and hazmat goods found damaged or leaking follow PR-09 plus PR-12 Cold-chain handling or PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. They are segregated immediately, cold-chain or spill controls applied, alarms and manual verifications logged, and the client notified the same shift. Hazmat never waits outside the 60 m2 ventilated cage.

11. All quarantine work is performed on supervised shifts — inbound operators, pickers, stock controllers and forklift operators moving goods, under the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. Work complies with site safety rules: 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles kept clear, physically separated 1.2 m walkways, and mandatory high-visibility vests, class S3 safety footwear and forklift seat belts when moving.

title: Returns Handling and Disposition
text:
1. We accept returns only in Zone F (600 m2) through a pre-booked return slot agreed with the client. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery to the end customer, counted from the delivery date on the dispatch record. Returns presented after 14 days, without authorisation, or without delivery and order reference will be held pending written client instruction and will not be inspected or booked.

2. All returns arrive as blocked, non-available stock. Drivers report to the designated check-in point and wait in the marked driver waiting area under dispatcher control. Returns are unloaded by trained staff in line with site safety rules and transferred directly to the returns inspection area in Zone F. They are never taken to Zones A, B, C, D or E before inspection.

3. Every return is booked on arrival as pending inspection in the warehouse management system under PR-07 Returns handling. Pending-inspection quantities are excluded from available stock, from replenishment of Zone C, from pick tasks and from dispatcher release. They are reported to the client only as pending inspection until final disposition.

4. We inspect every returned unit, not by sampling. Our returns and packing staff in Zone F check outer condition, seal and label integrity, quantity, SKU, batch, serial and expiry where applicable, sell-by condition for chilled goods, and reason for return against the return advice. Photographs are taken where practicable and retained with the inspection record.

5. Damaged, leaking, contaminated, temperature-abused or otherwise suspect returns found during inspection are segregated to quarantine in Zone F the same day they are found under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. They are booked as blocked, tagged with date, location found, SKU, quantity and reason, and notified to the client the same working day. They do not re-enter inspection until released by the shift supervisor.

6. After inspection of each return line, returns staff propose one of three dispositions only: restock to system stock, rework in Zone F packing, or scrap and write-off. No other disposition is used. No proposal is acted on without approval, and no adjustment is ever posted without a second count by a different person.

7. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of every inspected return on its shift. Restock is approved only where units, packaging, labelling, batch and expiry fully meet the client specification for saleable stock. Rework is approved only where repair, cleaning, re-labelling or re-packing under PR-05 can restore the goods to specification. All other goods are proposed for scrap.

8. Approved restock is re-labelled where needed, re-inspected, booked back to available stock in the system the same working day and released for put-away to Zone B, Zone E or the Zone F hazmat cage. Uninspected, unapproved or quarantined returns are never restocked and never reported as available.

9. Approved rework is completed in the Zone F value-added packing area by trained staff, then re-verified unit by unit before transfer. Only rework that passes re-verification is booked back to available stock. Failed rework is re-proposed for scrap. Rework requiring chilled control follows PR-12 and rework involving hazmat follows PR-13 inside the ventilated 60 m2 cage.

10. Goods confirmed as unsaleable are proposed for write-off and scrap. Write-off thresholds are fixed: the shift supervisor approves write-offs up to 500 EUR; any write-off above 500 EUR is approved only by the warehouse manager as accountable for the whole site. Approved scrapping is posted the same working day, reported in the daily outcome, weekly summary and monthly closing statement, and disposed of per client instruction.

11. All returns work is performed on supervised shifts, Monday to Friday 06:00–14:00 and 14:00–22:00, under the shift supervisor in charge of the floor. Work complies with site safety rules: 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings, 4.0 m main aisles and 3.0 m rack aisles kept clear, physically separated 1.2 m walkways, and mandatory high-visibility vests, class S3 safety footwear and forklift seat belts when moving.

title: Temperature-Controlled Storage
text:
1. Zone E (300 m2) is our only temperature-controlled storage. All client goods requiring chilled storage are held exclusively in Zone E under PR-12 Cold-chain handling. No chilled stock is held in Zones A, B, C, D or F, and no non-chilled goods are stored in Zone E to create space elsewhere.

2. We hold Zone E continuously between +2 °C and +8 °C while chilled goods are present. This range applies to storage, to handling inside Zone E, and to inspection, counting and rework performed on chilled goods. Exposure outside Zone E is minimised to the time strictly needed for movement, replenishment or loading.

3. Zone E is fitted with continuous temperature monitoring and audible and system alarms for deviation outside +2 °C to +8 °C, door-open overtime and equipment fault. Alarms are active on both operating shifts, Monday to Friday 06:00–14:00 and 14:00–22:00, and during any approved Saturday overtime when chilled stock is held.

4. In addition to automatic monitoring, we perform a manual temperature verification in Zone E on each shift. The shift supervisor ensures the check is taken with a calibrated device, logged with date, time, reading, location in Zone E and checker name, and retained with shift records. A missing or failed manual check is logged as an incident.

5. Only inspected goods booked into the warehouse management system in Zone A are put away to Zone E. Chilled inbound with temperature or cold-chain anomalies at intake is not booked as available, is notified to the client the same working day under PR-01, and is segregated to quarantine in Zone F the same day under PR-09 with cold-chain controls maintained where practicable.

6. Replenishment of chilled pick faces and picking of chilled orders follow the same scan-verified standard as ambient picks plus PR-12. Chilled quantities for current shifts are presented in designated chilled pick positions, picked against scanner tasks, scan-verified, packed and labelled without delay, and returned to Zone E or moved to Zone D staging with exposure minimised.

7. Outbound chilled loads are staged in Zone D only for their assigned door and immediate loading under PR-06. Wrapped, labelled chilled pallets are not held in Zone D beyond their booked slot, are not mixed with ambient loads unless the client has instructed it in writing, and are loaded only after dispatcher release with transport documents checked.

8. Any deviation is treated as suspect stock. Goods found damaged, wet, leaking or outside +2 °C to +8 °C during storage, counting, replenishment, picking, packing or alarm response are segregated immediately, quarantined in Zone F the same day under PR-09 plus PR-12, booked as blocked and excluded from available stock, replenishment and dispatcher release.

9. Every alarm, excursion or failed manual verification triggers same-shift response. The shift supervisor stops movements into and out of the affected part of Zone E, orders containment and re-check, ensures maintenance and calibration checks are logged by the maintenance technician, and notifies the client the same shift with time, duration, temperatures recorded, goods affected and disposition pending inspection.

10. Cycle counts in Zone E are performed under PR-08 on the rotating schedule with exposure minimised, and Zone E holdings are included separately in daily outcomes, the weekly summary and the monthly closing statement. Quarantined chilled goods are counted separately for control and reported only as blocked, never as available.

11. All Zone E work is performed on supervised shifts by trained staff under the shift supervisor in charge, with handling by checked equipment, 10 km/h inside and 5 km/h at pedestrian zones and crossings, physically separated 1.2 m walkways, and mandatory high-visibility vests, class S3 safety footwear and forklift seat belts when moving. The warehouse manager remains accountable for cold-chain integrity and final sign-offs.
